title.raw: 卷五十四 志第三十 禮八 Volume 54 Treatises 30: Rites 8

sentences.zh: 嘉禮二

translations.literal: Auspicious Rites Two
translations.idiomatic: Part Two: Auspicious Rites

sentences.zh: 冊皇后儀 冊妃嬪儀附 冊皇太子及皇太子妃儀 冊親王及王妃儀 冊公主儀附 皇帝加元服儀 冊皇太子皇子冠禮 品官冠禮 庶人冠禮

translations.literal: Rites for Investing the Empress; Rites for Investing Consorts (attached); Rites for Investing the Crown Prince and Crown Princess; Rites for Investing Princes and Princesses; Rites for Investing Imperial Princesses (attached); Rites for the Emperor's Capping Ceremony; Crowning Rites for the Crown Prince and Imperial Sons; Capping Rites for Officials of Rank; Capping Rites for Commoners
translations.idiomatic: Investing the Empress; Investing Consorts (supplementary); Investing the Crown Prince and Crown Princess; Investing Princes and Princesses; Investing Imperial Princesses (supplementary); The Emperor's Coming-of-Age Ceremony; Crowning the Crown Prince and Imperial Sons; Capping Rites for Ranked Officials; Capping Rites for Commoners

sentences.zh: 冊皇后儀

translations.literal: Rites for Investing the Empress
translations.idiomatic: Rites for Investing the Empress

sentences.zh: 古者立后無冊命禮。

translations.literal: In antiquity, establishing an empress had no investiture rite of written commission.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times there was no written commission ceremony when an empress was installed.

sentences.zh: 至漢靈帝立宋美人爲皇后，始御殿，命太尉持節，奉璽綬，讀冊。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ling of Han established the Beautiful Lady Song as empress, for the first time he attended the hall, ordered the Grand Marshal to hold the tally of authority, present the imperial seal and sash, and read the commission document.
translations.idiomatic: It was only under Emperor Ling of Han, when he installed the Beautiful Lady Song as empress, that the emperor first appeared in the hall and ordered the Grand Marshal to hold the imperial tally, present the seal and sash, and read the investiture document aloud.

sentences.zh: 皇后北面稱臣妾，跪受。

translations.literal: The empress faced north, called herself subject and consort, and knelt to receive it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress faced north, addressed herself as the emperor's subject and consort, and knelt to receive the commission.

sentences.zh: 其後沿爲定制，而儀文代各不同。

translations.literal: Thereafter this was followed as a fixed regulation, yet the ritual texts differed in each age.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter this became the established custom, though the ritual procedures varied from dynasty to dynasty.

sentences.zh: 明儀注大抵參唐、宋之制而用之，太祖初，定制。

translations.literal: The Ming ritual regulations largely drew on the Tang and Song systems and applied them; in the beginning of the Taizu reign, the regulations were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming ritual code largely followed and adapted the Tang and Song systems; Taizu established the definitive regulations at the dynasty's founding.

sentences.zh: 凡冊皇后，前期三日齋戒，遣官祭告天地、宗廟。

translations.literal: Whenever an empress was to be invested, three days beforehand there was fasting and purification, and officials were dispatched to offer sacrifices and announce it to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an empress was to be invested, the court observed three days of fasting and purification beforehand and dispatched officials to announce the event to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 前一日，侍儀司設冊寶案於奉天殿御座前，設奉節官位於冊案之東，掌節者位於其左，稍退，設承制官位於其南，俱西向。

translations.literal: On the day before, the Directorate of Ceremonial Attendants set the commission and seal tables before the imperial throne in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, placed the Bearer of the Tally east of the commission table, the Tally Keeper to his left slightly withdrawn, and the Edict Receiver to the south, all facing west.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the ceremony, the Directorate of Ceremonial Attendants placed the tables for the commission document and imperial seal before the throne in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, positioned the Bearer of the Tally east of the commission table with the Tally Keeper to his left at a slight remove, and placed the Edict Receiver to the south—all facing west.

sentences.zh: 設正副使受制位於橫街於南，北向。

translations.literal: The positions for the chief and deputy envoys to receive the edict were set south of the transverse street, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: South of the transverse avenue, positions were set for the chief and deputy envoys to receive the imperial edict, both facing north.

sentences.zh: 設承制宣制官位於其北，設奉節奉冊奉寶官位於其東北，俱西向。

translations.literal: The position for the edict proclaimer was set to their north, and the positions for the tally bearer, commission bearer, and seal bearer were set to their northeast, all facing west.
translations.idiomatic: North of them stood the edict proclaimer; to their northeast stood the tally bearer, commission bearer, and seal bearer—all facing west.

sentences.zh: 設正副使受冊寶褥位於受制位之北，北向。

translations.literal: The cushioned positions for the chief and deputy envoys to receive the commission and seal were set north of the edict-reception positions, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: North of the edict-reception positions, cushioned places were prepared where the chief and deputy envoys would receive the commission and seal, both facing north.

sentences.zh: 典儀二人位丹陛上南，贊禮二人位正副使北，知班二人位贊禮之南，俱東西相向。

translations.literal: Two masters of ceremony stood south on the red steps, two ritual announcers stood north of the chief and deputy envoys, and two ushers stood south of the announcers, all facing one another east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Two masters of ceremony stood on the southern part of the red steps; two ritual announcers stood north of the chief and deputy envoys; and two ushers stood south of the announcers—all arranged facing one another across the east-west axis.

sentences.zh: 百官及侍從位，如朝儀。

translations.literal: The positions of the hundred officials and attendants followed the audience rite.
translations.idiomatic: The positions of officials and attendants followed the usual court audience arrangement.

sentences.zh: 是日早，列鹵簿，陳甲士，設樂如儀。

translations.literal: Early that day, the imperial guard of honor was arrayed, armored soldiers were deployed, and music was set up according to the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Early that morning the imperial guard of honor was drawn up, armored troops were posted, and the musical ensemble was arranged according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 內官設皇后受冊位及冊節寶案於宮中，設香案於殿上，設權置冊寶案於香案前，設女樂於丹陛。

translations.literal: Inside the palace, inner officials set the empress's position for receiving the commission and the tables for the tally, commission, and seal; an incense table was set in the hall; a provisional table for the commission and seal was set before the incense table; and female musicians were placed on the red steps.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace, inner officials prepared the empress's place for receiving the commission, the tables for tally, commission, and seal, an incense table in the hall, a provisional table for the commission and seal before the incense table, and female musicians on the red steps.

sentences.zh: 質明，正副使及百官入。

translations.literal: At dawn, the chief and deputy envoys and the hundred officials entered.
translations.idiomatic: At first light the chief and deputy envoys and all officials entered.

sentences.zh: 鼓三嚴，皇帝袞冕御奉天殿。

translations.literal: The drum sounded three rounds of vigil, and the emperor in full ceremonial robes attended the Hall of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: After the triple drum signal marking the third watch of vigil, the emperor in full ceremonial robes took his place in the Hall of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 禮部官奉冊寶，各置於案。

translations.literal: Officials of the Ministry of Rites presented the commission and seal, each placed on its table.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of Rites officials presented the commission document and imperial seal, placing each upon its table.

sentences.zh: 諸執事官各人就殿上位立。

translations.literal: All officiating officials each took their positions in the hall and stood.
translations.idiomatic: Each officiating official took up his assigned position in the hall.

sentences.zh: 樂作，四拜，興，樂止。

translations.literal: Music began; four prostrations; they rose; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Music began; the envoys performed four prostrations, then rose; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 承制官奏發皇后冊寶，承制訖，由中門出，降自中陛，至宣制位，曰：「有制」。

translations.literal: The edict receiver memorialized to issue the empress's commission and seal; when the edict was received, he went out through the central gate, descended by the central steps, reached the proclamation position, and said, "There is an edict."
translations.idiomatic: The edict receiver memorialized for permission to issue the empress's commission and seal; once the edict was granted, he left through the central gate, descended the central steps, and at the proclamation position announced, "By imperial command."

sentences.zh: 正副使跪，承制官宣制曰：「冊妃某氏爲皇后，命卿等持節展禮。

translations.literal: The chief and deputy envoys knelt; the edict proclaimer proclaimed: "Invest Consort So-and-so as empress; I command you to hold the tally and carry out the rite."
translations.idiomatic: The chief and deputy envoys knelt as the edict proclaimer announced: "Consort So-and-so is invested as empress. You are commanded to bear the imperial tally and perform the ceremony."

sentences.zh: 」宣畢，由殿西門入。

translations.literal: " When the proclamation was finished, he entered through the western gate of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the proclamation was complete, he re-entered through the hall's western gate.

sentences.zh: 正副使俯伏，興。

translations.literal: The chief and deputy envoys bowed low, then rose.
translations.idiomatic: The chief and deputy envoys bowed low to the ground and then rose.

sentences.zh: 執事者舉冊寶案，由中門出，降自中陛。

translations.literal: The attendants raised the tables for the commission and seal, went out through the central gate, and descended by the central steps.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants lifted the tables bearing the commission and seal, passed through the central gate, and descended the central steps.

sentences.zh: 奉節官率掌節者前導，至正副使褥位，以案置於北。

translations.literal: The tally bearer led the tally keeper forward as guides, reached the cushioned positions of the chief and deputy envoys, and placed the tables to the north.
translations.idiomatic: The tally bearer led the tally keeper forward to the cushioned positions of the chief and deputy envoys and set the tables to the north.

sentences.zh: 掌節者脫節衣，以節授奉節官。

translations.literal: The tally keeper removed the tally garment and handed the tally to the tally bearer.
translations.idiomatic: The tally keeper removed the ceremonial tally garment and handed the tally to the tally bearer.

sentences.zh: 奉節官以授正使，正使以授掌節者，掌節者跪受，興，立於正使之左。

translations.literal: The tally bearer handed it to the chief envoy; the chief envoy handed it to the tally keeper; the tally keeper knelt to receive it, rose, and stood to the left of the chief envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The tally bearer passed it to the chief envoy, who passed it back to the tally keeper; the tally keeper knelt to receive it, rose, and stood at the chief envoy's left.

sentences.zh: 奉節官退。

translations.literal: The tally bearer withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The tally bearer withdrew.

sentences.zh: 引禮引正使詣受冊位，奉冊官以冊授正使，正使跪受，置於案。

translations.literal: The usher led the chief envoy to the position for receiving the commission; the commission bearer handed the commission to the chief envoy; the chief envoy knelt to receive it and placed it on the table.
translations.idiomatic: The usher guided the chief envoy to the commission-reception position; the commission bearer handed him the document; the chief envoy knelt to receive it and set it on the table.

sentences.zh: 退，復位。

translations.literal: He withdrew and returned to his position.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew and returned to his place.

sentences.zh: 副使受寶亦如之。

translations.literal: The deputy envoy received the seal in the same manner.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy envoy received the seal in the same way.

sentences.zh: 樂作，正副使四拜。

translations.literal: Music began; the chief and deputy envoys performed four prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: Music began, and the chief and deputy envoys performed four prostrations.

sentences.zh: 興，樂止。

translations.literal: They rose; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: They rose, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 正使隨冊，副使隨寶，掌節者前導，舉案者次之，樂作。

translations.literal: The chief envoy followed the commission, the deputy envoy followed the seal, the tally keeper led the way, and those bearing the tables came next; music began.
translations.idiomatic: The chief envoy bore the commission, the deputy envoy the seal, the tally keeper led the procession, and the table bearers followed; music began.

sentences.zh: 出奉天門，樂止。

translations.literal: They went out through the Gate of Supreme Harmony; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: They passed out through the Gate of Supreme Harmony, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 侍儀奏禮畢，駕興，百官出。

translations.literal: The ceremonial attendant memorialized that the rite was complete; the imperial carriage rose; the hundred officials departed.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial attendant announced that the rite was complete; the emperor's carriage departed; and the officials left.

sentences.zh: 掌節者加節衣，奉冊寶官皆搢笏，取冊寶置龍亭內，儀仗大樂前導，至中宮門外，樂作。

translations.literal: The tally keeper put on the tally garment; all commission and seal bearers inserted their tablets; they took the commission and seal and placed them in the dragon pavilion; guards of honor and great music led the way to outside the gate of the inner palace; music began.
translations.idiomatic: The tally keeper donned the tally garment; the commission and seal bearers tucked their court tablets into their belts; the commission and seal were placed in the dragon pavilion; and with guards of honor and ceremonial music leading the way, the procession reached the gate of the inner palace, where music began again.

sentences.zh: 皇后具九龍四鳳冠，服禕衣，出閤，至殿上，南向立。

translations.literal: The empress wore the nine-dragon four-phoenix crown and ceremonial robe, came out of her chambers, reached the hall, and stood facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Wearing the nine-dragon four-phoenix crown and ceremonial robe, the empress emerged from her chambers, came to the hall, and stood facing south.

sentences.zh: 樂止，正副使奉冊寶權置於門外所設案上。

translations.literal: Music ceased; the chief and deputy envoys provisionally placed the commission and seal on the tables set outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: The music stopped, and the chief and deputy envoys temporarily set the commission and seal on the tables prepared outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 引禮引正副使及內使監令俱就位。

translations.literal: The usher led the chief and deputy envoys and the director of the inner palace eunuchs all to take their positions.
translations.idiomatic: The usher guided the chief and deputy envoys and the director of the inner palace eunuchs to their positions.

sentences.zh: 正使詣內使監令前，稱冊禮使臣某，副使臣某，奉制授皇后冊寶。

translations.literal: The chief envoy went before the director of the inner palace eunuchs and declared: "Commission-rite envoy So-and-so, deputy envoy So-and-so, by imperial command present the commission and seal to the empress."
translations.idiomatic: The chief envoy approached the director of the inner palace eunuchs and announced: "Commission envoy So-and-so and deputy envoy So-and-so, by imperial command, present the commission and seal to Her Majesty the Empress."

sentences.zh: 內使監令入告皇后，出，復位。

translations.literal: The director of the inner palace eunuchs entered to inform the empress, came out, and returned to his position.
translations.idiomatic: The director entered to inform the empress, then came out and returned to his place.

sentences.zh: 引禮引內外命婦入就位。

translations.literal: The usher led the inner and outer titled ladies in to take their positions.
translations.idiomatic: The usher led the titled ladies of the inner and outer courts to their positions.

sentences.zh: 正使奉冊授內使監令，內使監令跪受，以授內官。

translations.literal: The chief envoy presented the commission to the director of the inner palace eunuchs; the director knelt to receive it and handed it to an inner official.
translations.idiomatic: The chief envoy presented the commission to the director, who knelt to receive it and passed it to an inner palace official.

sentences.zh: 副使授寶亦如之。

translations.literal: The deputy envoy presented the seal in the same manner.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy envoy presented the seal in the same way.

sentences.zh: 各復位。

translations.literal: Each returned to his position.
translations.idiomatic: Each returned to his place.

sentences.zh: 內使監令率奉冊奉寶內官入，各置於案。

translations.literal: The director of the inner palace eunuchs led the inner officials bearing the commission and seal in, and each item was placed on its table.
translations.idiomatic: The director led the inner officials bearing the commission and seal into the hall, where each was set upon its table.

sentences.zh: 尚儀引皇后降陛，詣庭中位立。

translations.literal: The chief mistress of ceremony led the empress down the steps to stand at the position in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The chief mistress of ceremony guided the empress down the steps to stand at her place in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 內官奉冊寶立於皇后之東西。

translations.literal: Inner officials bearing the commission and seal stood to the east and west of the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Inner officials holding the commission and seal stood to the east and west of the empress.

sentences.zh: 內使監令稱「有制」，尚儀奏拜。

translations.literal: The director of the inner palace eunuchs declared, "There is an edict"; the chief mistress of ceremony memorialized to prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: The director announced, "By imperial command," and the chief mistress of ceremony called for obeisance.

sentences.zh: 皇后拜，樂作。

translations.literal: The empress prostrated herself; music began.
translations.idiomatic: The empress prostrated herself as music began.

sentences.zh: 四拜，興，樂止。

translations.literal: Four prostrations; she rose; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: She performed four prostrations, then rose; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 宣制訖，奉冊內官以冊授讀冊內官讀訖，以授內使監令。

translations.literal: When the proclamation was finished, the inner official bearing the commission handed the commission to the inner official who read the commission; when the reading was finished, he handed it to the director of the inner palace eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: After the edict was proclaimed, the inner official bearing the commission handed it to the reader; once the reading was complete, it was passed to the director of the inner palace eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 內使監令跪以授皇后，皇后跪受，以授司言。

translations.literal: The director knelt and handed it to the empress; the empress knelt to receive it and handed it to the Mistress of Speech.
translations.idiomatic: The director knelt and presented it to the empress, who knelt to receive it and passed it to the Mistress of Speech.

sentences.zh: 奉寶如前儀。

translations.literal: Presenting the seal followed the preceding rite.
translations.idiomatic: The presentation of the seal followed the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 受訖，以授司寶。

translations.literal: When she had received it, she handed it to the Mistress of the Seal.
translations.idiomatic: Once she had received it, she passed it to the Mistress of the Seal.

sentences.zh: 尚儀奏拜，皇后拜如前。

translations.literal: The chief mistress of ceremony memorialized to prostrate; the empress prostrated herself as before.
translations.idiomatic: The chief mistress of ceremony called for obeisance, and the empress prostrated herself as before.

sentences.zh: 內使監令出，詣正副使前，稱 「皇后受冊禮畢」。

translations.literal: The director of the inner palace eunuchs came out, went before the chief and deputy envoys, and declared, "The empress's reception of the commission rite is complete."
translations.idiomatic: The director came out, approached the chief and deputy envoys, and announced, "Her Majesty has completed the reception of the commission."

sentences.zh: 使者退詣奉天殿橫街南，北面西上立，給事中立於正副使東北，西向。

translations.literal: The envoys withdrew and went south of the transverse street of the Hall of Supreme Harmony, stood facing north ascending from the west, and the supervising secretary stood northeast of the chief and deputy envoys, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys withdrew to the south side of the transverse avenue before the Hall of Supreme Harmony and stood facing north from the western ascent; the supervising secretary stood northeast of them, facing west.

sentences.zh: 正副使再拜覆命曰：「奉制冊命皇后禮畢。

translations.literal: The chief and deputy envoys prostrated themselves again and reported: "By imperial command, the rite of investing the empress is complete."
translations.idiomatic: The chief and deputy envoys prostrated themselves again and reported: "By imperial command, the ceremony of investing the empress is complete."

sentences.zh: 」又再拜，給事中奏聞，乃退。

translations.literal: " They prostrated themselves again; the supervising secretary memorialized to inform the throne; then they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They prostrated themselves once more; the supervising secretary memorialized to inform the emperor; then they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 皇后既受冊寶，升座。

translations.literal: After the empress had received the commission and seal, she ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving the commission and seal, the empress took her seat upon the throne.

sentences.zh: 引禮引內命婦班首一人，詣殿中賀位跪，致詞曰：「茲遇皇后殿下膺受冊寶，正位中宮，妾等不勝歡慶，謹奉賀。

translations.literal: The usher led the leading lady among the inner titled ladies to the congratulatory position in the hall, where she knelt and delivered the address: "Now that Her Majesty has received the commission and seal and taken the central position of the inner palace, we cannot contain our joy and respectfully offer congratulations."
translations.idiomatic: The usher led the senior inner titled lady to the congratulatory position in the hall, where she knelt and said: "Now that Your Majesty has received the commission and seal and assumed the central place in the inner palace, we are overcome with joy and respectfully offer our congratulations."

sentences.zh: 」贊拜，樂作。

translations.literal: " The announcer called for prostration; music began.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer called for obeisance, and music began.

sentences.zh: 再拜，興，樂止。

translations.literal: Two prostrations; they rose; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: They performed two prostrations, then rose; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 退，復位。

translations.literal: They withdrew and returned to their positions.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew and returned to their places.

sentences.zh: 又引外命婦班首一人，入就殿上賀位，如內命婦儀。

translations.literal: Again the usher led the leading lady among the outer titled ladies in to take the congratulatory position in the hall, following the inner titled ladies' rite.
translations.idiomatic: The usher then led the senior outer titled lady in to take the congratulatory position in the hall, following the same procedure as the inner ladies.

sentences.zh: 禮畢俱出。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, all departed.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony was finished, all withdrew.

sentences.zh: 皇后降座，樂作。

translations.literal: The empress descended from the throne; music began.
translations.idiomatic: The empress left her throne as music began.

sentences.zh: 還閤，樂止。

translations.literal: She returned to her chambers; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: She returned to her chambers, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 次日，百官上表箋稱賀。

translations.literal: On the following day, the hundred officials submitted memorials and petitions offering congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, officials submitted congratulatory memorials and petitions.

sentences.zh: 皇帝御殿受賀，如常儀。

translations.literal: The emperor attended the hall to receive congratulations, following the usual rite.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received congratulations in the hall according to the usual ceremony.

sentences.zh: 遂卜日，行謁廟禮，先遣官用牲牢行事，告以皇后將祗見之意。

translations.literal: Then a day was divined, and the temple-visitation rite was performed; officials were first dispatched to offer ox and sheep sacrifices and announce that the empress would reverently attend.
translations.idiomatic: A day was then chosen for the temple-visitation rite; officials were first dispatched to offer full sacrificial victims and announce that the empress would soon pay her reverent visit.

sentences.zh: 前期，皇后齋三日，內外命婦及執事內官齋一日。

translations.literal: Beforehand, the empress fasted for three days; inner and outer titled ladies and officiating inner officials fasted for one day.
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand the empress observed three days of fasting, while titled ladies of the inner and outer courts and officiating inner officials fasted for one day.

sentences.zh: 設皇后拜位於廟門外及廟中，設內命婦陪祀位於廟庭南，外命婦陪祀位於內命婦之南。

translations.literal: The empress's prostration positions were set outside the temple gate and inside the temple; the inner titled ladies' attendant-sacrifice positions were set south in the temple courtyard; the outer titled ladies' attendant-sacrifice positions were set south of the inner titled ladies.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's places for obeisance were set outside the temple gate and within the temple; the inner titled ladies' attendant positions were set in the southern part of the temple courtyard; and the outer titled ladies' positions were set south of them.

sentences.zh: 司贊位皇后拜位之東西，司賓位內命婦之北，司香位香案右。

translations.literal: The announcer stood east and west of the empress's prostration position; the usher stood north of the inner titled ladies; the incense officer stood to the right of the incense table.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer stood to the east and west of the empress's obeisance position; the usher stood north of the inner titled ladies; and the incense officer stood to the right of the incense table.

sentences.zh: 陳盥洗於階東，司盥洗官位其所。

translations.literal: Hand-washing vessels were displayed east of the steps, and the hand-washing officer stood at that place.
translations.idiomatic: Hand-washing vessels were set out east of the steps, with the hand-washing officer at his station there.

sentences.zh: 至日，內外命婦各翟衣集中宮內門外。

translations.literal: On the appointed day, inner and outer titled ladies each in pheasant robes assembled outside the inner gate of the central palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day, titled ladies of the inner and outer courts assembled outside the inner gate of the central palace, each wearing her pheasant robe.

sentences.zh: 皇后具九龍四鳳冠，服禕衣。

translations.literal: The empress wore the nine-dragon four-phoenix crown and ceremonial robe.
translations.idiomatic: The empress wore the nine-dragon four-phoenix crown and ceremonial robe.

sentences.zh: 出內宮門，升輿，至外門外降輿，升重翟車。

translations.literal: She went out through the inner palace gate, ascended the palanquin, reached outside the outer gate and descended from the palanquin, and ascended the double-pheasant carriage.
translations.idiomatic: She left through the inner palace gate, entered her palanquin, descended outside the outer gate, and mounted the double-pheasant carriage.

sentences.zh: 鼓吹設而不作。

translations.literal: The ceremonial band was set up but did not play.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial band was posted but did not play.

sentences.zh: 尚儀陳儀衛，次外命婦，次內命婦，皆乘車前導。

translations.literal: The chief mistress of ceremony arrayed the guard of honor; next came the outer titled ladies; next the inner titled ladies; all rode in carriages leading the way.
translations.idiomatic: The chief mistress of ceremony arranged the guard of honor, followed by the outer titled ladies in their carriages, then the inner titled ladies—all proceeding ahead as guides.

sentences.zh: 內使監扈從，宿衛陳兵仗前後導從。

translations.literal: The director of the inner palace eunuchs escorted her; the palace guard arrayed weapons before and behind as guides and escorts.
translations.idiomatic: The director of the inner palace eunuchs attended her, while palace guards with arms arrayed marched before and behind as escort.

sentences.zh: 皇后至廟門，司賓引命婦先入。

translations.literal: When the empress reached the temple gate, the usher led the titled ladies in first.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress reached the temple gate, the usher led the titled ladies in ahead of her.

sentences.zh: 皇后降車，司贊導自左門入，就位，北向立。

translations.literal: The empress descended from the carriage; the announcer guided her in through the left gate, she took her position, and stood facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The empress descended from her carriage; the announcer guided her in through the left gate to her position, where she stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 命婦各就位，北向立。

translations.literal: The titled ladies each took their positions and stood facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Each titled lady took her place and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 司贊奏拜，司賓贊拜，皇后及命婦皆再拜，興。

translations.literal: The announcer memorialized to prostrate; the usher called for prostration; the empress and titled ladies all performed two prostrations and rose.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer called for obeisance, the usher echoed the call, and the empress and titled ladies all performed two prostrations and rose.

sentences.zh: 司贊請詣盥洗位，盥手帨抉手，由東陛升，至神位前。

translations.literal: The announcer requested that they proceed to the hand-washing position; they washed their hands, dried them with the towel, and ascended by the eastern steps to before the spirit tablet.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer directed them to the hand-washing station; they washed and dried their hands, ascended the eastern steps, and came before the spirit tablet.

sentences.zh: 司贊奏上香者三，司香捧香於右，皇后三上訖，導復位，贊拜如前。

translations.literal: The announcer memorialized to offer incense three times; the incense officer held incense on the right; the empress offered incense three times and finished; they were guided back to their positions; prostration was called as before.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer called for three offerings of incense; the incense officer held the incense to the right; the empress offered incense three times; they were guided back to their places; and obeisance was called as before.

sentences.zh: 司贊奏禮畢，皇后出自廟之左門，命婦以次出。

translations.literal: The announcer memorialized that the rite was complete; the empress went out through the left gate of the temple; the titled ladies departed in order.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer declared the rite complete; the empress left through the temple's left gate, and the titled ladies withdrew in turn.

sentences.zh: 皇后升車，命婦前導，如來儀。

translations.literal: The empress ascended the carriage; the titled ladies led the way as on the coming journey.
translations.idiomatic: The empress mounted her carriage, with the titled ladies leading the way as on the outward journey.

sentences.zh: 過廟，鼓吹振作，皇后入宮。

translations.literal: After passing the temple, the ceremonial band played vigorously; the empress entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Once past the temple, the ceremonial band struck up, and the empress returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 是日，皇帝宴羣臣于謹身殿，皇后宴內外命婦於中宮。

translations.literal: That day, the emperor banqueted the officials in the Hall of Cultivating the Person; the empress banqueted inner and outer titled ladies in the central palace.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor hosted a banquet for officials in the Hall of Cultivating the Person, while the empress hosted inner and outer titled ladies in the central palace.

sentences.zh: 皆如正旦宴會儀。

translations.literal: All followed the New Year's Day banquet rite.
translations.idiomatic: Both banquets followed the New Year's Day feast ceremony.

sentences.zh: 及成祖即位，冊皇后徐氏，其制小異。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne and invested Empress Xu, the regulations differed slightly.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne and invested Empress Xu, the procedure differed slightly.

sentences.zh: 皇帝皮弁服御華蓋殿，翰林院官以詔書用寶訖，然後御奉天殿，傳制皇后受冊。

translations.literal: The emperor in the leather cap and court dress attended the Hall of Flowering Canopy; Hanlin Academy officials applied the seal to the edict; then he attended the Hall of Supreme Harmony and transmitted the edict for the empress to receive the commission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in leather cap and court dress took his place in the Hall of Flowering Canopy while Hanlin officials sealed the edict; he then proceeded to the Hall of Supreme Harmony to issue the command for the empress to receive her commission.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，翰林官以詔書授禮部官，禮部官奉詔書於承天門開讀。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, Hanlin officials handed the edict to Ministry of Rites officials; Ministry of Rites officials presented the edict at the Gate of Receiving Heaven and had it read aloud.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony was finished, Hanlin officials handed the edict to the Ministry of Rites, whose officials presented it at the Gate of Receiving Heaven for public reading.

sentences.zh: 皇帝還宮，率皇后具服詣奉先殿謁告畢。

translations.literal: The emperor returned to the palace, led the empress in full ceremonial dress to the Hall of Imperial Ancestors to pay reverent announcement, and finished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned to the palace and, with the empress in full ceremonial dress, paid a reverent visit of announcement at the Hall of Imperial Ancestors.

sentences.zh: 皇后具服於內殿，俟皇帝升座。

translations.literal: The empress in full ceremonial dress waited in the inner hall for the emperor to ascend the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The empress, in full ceremonial dress, waited in the inner hall for the emperor to take his seat.

sentences.zh: 贊引女官導詣拜位，行謝恩禮，樂作。

translations.literal: The announcer led female officials to guide her to the prostration position; she performed the thanksgiving rite; music began.
translations.idiomatic: Female officials guided her to the obeisance position to perform the thanksgiving rite as music began.

sentences.zh: 八拜，興，樂止。

translations.literal: Eight prostrations; she rose; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: She performed eight prostrations, then rose; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 禮畢。

translations.literal: The rite was complete.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremony was finished.

sentences.zh: 次日，皇帝皇后受賀宴會，如前儀。

translations.literal: On the following day, the emperor and empress received congratulations and banquets, as in the preceding rite.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor and empress received congratulations and hosted banquets according to the earlier procedure.

sentences.zh: 天順八年，增定親王於皇帝前慶賀，次詣皇太后慶賀，次詣皇后前八拜儀。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianshun, it was added and fixed that princes offered congratulations before the emperor, next went to offer congratulations to the empress dowager, and next went before the empress to perform the eight-prostration rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Tianshun reign, regulations were added requiring princes to offer congratulations before the emperor, then before the empress dowager, and then to perform eight prostrations before the empress.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十三年，冊皇后方氏，禮臣具儀注，有謁告內殿儀，無謁告太廟世廟之禮，帝命議增。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiajing, when Empress Fang was invested, ritual officials prepared the regulations, which included the rite of reverent announcement in the inner hall but not the rite of reverent announcement at the Grand Ancestral Temple and the Imperial Ancestral Temple; the emperor ordered discussion to add them.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Jiajing, when Empress Fang was invested, ritual officials drew up regulations that included announcement in the inner hall but not at the Grand Ancestral Temple or Imperial Ancestral Temple; the emperor ordered them to propose additions.

sentences.zh: 於是禮臣以儀上。

translations.literal: Thereupon the ritual officials submitted the rite.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials thereupon submitted the revised ceremony.

sentences.zh: 先期齋三日，所司陳設如時祫儀。

translations.literal: Beforehand there was fasting for three days; the responsible offices set out arrangements as in the seasonal combined-sacrifice rite.
translations.idiomatic: Three days of fasting were observed beforehand, and the responsible offices arranged the setting according to the seasonal combined-sacrifice ceremony.

sentences.zh: 至日，皇帝御輅，皇后妃御翟車，同詣太廟。

translations.literal: On the appointed day, the emperor rode the imperial carriage, the empress and consorts rode the pheasant carriage, and together they went to the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day the emperor rode in the imperial carriage while the empress and consorts rode in pheasant carriages, and all proceeded together to the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 命官奉七廟主升神座訖。

translations.literal: Officials were ordered to present the spirit tablets of the seven temples and raise them to the spirit seats; this was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were ordered to present the spirit tablets from the seven temples and install them upon the spirit seats.

sentences.zh: 皇帝奉高皇帝主，皇后奉高皇后主，出升神座。

translations.literal: The emperor presented the tablet of the Gaozu Emperor; the empress presented the tablet of the Gaohou Empress; they went out and raised them to the spirit seats.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bore the tablet of the Hongwu Emperor and the empress bore the tablet of his empress; together they installed them upon the spirit seats.

sentences.zh: 迎神、上香、奠帛、祼獻，樂作止，皆如儀。

translations.literal: Welcoming the spirit, offering incense, presenting silks, and libation offering; music beginning and ceasing—all followed the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the spirits, offering incense, presenting silks, and pouring libations, with music beginning and stopping—all followed the prescribed ceremony.

sentences.zh: 次詣世廟行禮，同上儀。

translations.literal: Next they went to the Imperial Ancestral Temple to perform the rite, the same as the above rite.
translations.idiomatic: They next proceeded to the Imperial Ancestral Temple and performed the same ceremony.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年增定，頒詔次日，命婦行見皇后禮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing it was added and fixed that on the day after the edict was promulgated, titled ladies performed the audience rite with the empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longqing a further regulation was added: on the day after the edict was promulgated, titled ladies performed the audience ceremony with the empress.

sentences.zh: 冊妃之儀

translations.literal: Rites for investing a consort
translations.idiomatic: Rites for Investing a Consort

sentences.zh: 自洪武三年冊孫氏爲貴妃，定皇帝不御殿，承制官宣制曰：「妃某氏，特封某妃，命卿等持節行禮。

translations.literal: From the third year of Hongwu, when Lady Sun was invested as honored consort, it was fixed that the emperor did not attend the hall; the edict proclaimer proclaimed: "Consort So-and-so is specially enfeoffed as such-and-such consort; I command you to hold the tally and carry out the rite."
translations.idiomatic: From the third year of Hongwu, when Lady Sun was invested as honored consort, it was established that the emperor did not appear in the hall; the edict proclaimer announced: "Consort So-and-so is specially enfeoffed with the title of such-and-such consort. You are commanded to bear the imperial tally and perform the ceremony."

sentences.zh: 」但授冊，無寶，餘並如中宮儀。

translations.literal: " Only the commission was conferred, without a seal; the rest all followed the central palace rite.
translations.idiomatic: Only the commission document was conferred, without an imperial seal; otherwise the procedure followed that for the central palace.

sentences.zh: 永樂七年，定冊妃禮。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongle, the rite for investing a consort was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yongle the ceremony for investing a consort was formally established.

sentences.zh: 皇帝皮弁服御華蓋殿，傳制。

translations.literal: The emperor in leather cap and court dress attended the Hall of Flowering Canopy and transmitted the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, wearing leather cap and court dress, took his place in the Hall of Flowering Canopy and issued the command.

sentences.zh: 至宣宗立孫貴妃，始授寶，憲宗封萬貴妃，始稱皇，非洪武之舊矣。

translations.literal: When the Xuande Emperor established Honored Consort Sun, a seal was first conferred; when the Chenghua Emperor enfeoffed Honored Consort Wan, she was first called "imperial"—no longer the Hongwu precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xuande Emperor, when Honored Consort Sun was installed, an imperial seal was conferred for the first time; under the Chenghua Emperor, when Honored Consort Wan was enfeoffed, she was first styled "imperial"—a departure from Hongwu practice.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十年，帝冊九嬪，禮官上儀注。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiajing, the emperor invested nine imperial concubines; ritual officials submitted the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Jiajing the emperor invested nine imperial concubines, and ritual officials submitted the ceremonial regulations.

sentences.zh: 先日，所司陳設儀仗如朔望儀。

translations.literal: On the day before, the responsible offices set out guards of honor as in the new- and full-moon rite.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the ceremony the responsible offices arrayed guards of honor as on the new- and full-moon occasions.

sentences.zh: 至期，皇帝具袞冕，告太廟、世廟訖，易皮弁服，御華蓋殿。

translations.literal: When the day arrived, the emperor in full ceremonial robes announced at the Grand Ancestral Temple and Imperial Ancestral Temple; when finished, he changed to leather cap and court dress and attended the Hall of Flowering Canopy.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day the emperor in full ceremonial robes announced the event at the Grand Ancestral Temple and Imperial Ancestral Temple; afterward he changed into leather cap and court dress and took his place in the Hall of Flowering Canopy.

sentences.zh: 百官公服入行禮。

translations.literal: The hundred officials in court dress entered to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in court dress entered to perform the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 正、副使朝服承制，舉節冊至九嬪宮。

translations.literal: The chief and deputy envoys in court dress received the edict, raised the tally and commission, and went to the palace of the nine imperial concubines.
translations.idiomatic: The chief and deputy envoys, in court dress, received the imperial command and bore the tally and commission to the palace of the nine imperial concubines.

sentences.zh: 九嬪迎於宮門外，隨至拜位。

translations.literal: The nine imperial concubines welcomed them outside the palace gate and followed to the prostration position.
translations.idiomatic: The nine imperial concubines welcomed them outside the palace gate and proceeded to the obeisance position.

sentences.zh: 女官宣冊，九嬪受冊，先後八拜。

translations.literal: Female officials proclaimed the commission; the nine imperial concubines received the commission and performed eight prostrations in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Female officials read the commission aloud; the nine imperial concubines received it and performed eight prostrations in turn.

sentences.zh: 送節出宮門覆命。

translations.literal: They sent back the tally, went out through the palace gate, and reported completion of the mission.
translations.idiomatic: They returned the tally, left through the palace gate, and reported back that the mission was complete.

sentences.zh: 九嬪隨具服候，皇后率詣奉先殿謁告，及詣皇帝、皇后前謝恩，俱如冊妃禮。

translations.literal: The nine imperial concubines then put on full ceremonial dress and waited; the empress led them to the Hall of Imperial Ancestors for reverent announcement, and to before the emperor and empress for thanksgiving—all as in the consort-investiture rite.
translations.idiomatic: The nine imperial concubines then donned full ceremonial dress; the empress led them to announce the event at the Hall of Imperial Ancestors and to offer thanks before the emperor and empress—all following the consort-investiture procedure.

sentences.zh: 惟圭用次玉，谷文、銀冊少殺於皇妃五分之一。

translations.literal: Only the scepter used secondary jade with grain pattern; the silver commission was one-fifth less than that for an honored imperial consort.
translations.idiomatic: Their scepters were of secondary jade with grain-pattern ornament, and their silver commission documents were one-fifth smaller than those for honored imperial consorts.

sentences.zh: 二十年，冊德妃張氏，以妃將就室，而帝方靜攝，不傳制，不謁告內殿，餘並如舊。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, when Virtuous Consort Zhang was invested, because the consort was about to enter her chamber while the emperor was in quiet regency, no edict was transmitted and no reverent announcement was made in the inner hall; the rest followed the old practice.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, when Virtuous Consort Zhang was invested, the emperor was in quiet regency and the consort was about to take up residence; no edict was transmitted and no announcement was made in the inner hall, but otherwise the old procedure was followed.

sentences.zh: 冊皇太子及皇太子妃儀

translations.literal: Rites for investing the crown prince and crown princess
translations.idiomatic: Rites for Investing the Crown Prince and Crown Princess

sentences.zh: 自漢代始稱皇太子，明帝始有臨軒、冊拜之儀。

translations.literal: From the Han dynasty the title crown prince was first used; under Emperor Ming there first appeared the rite of attending the hall and investiture prostration.
translations.idiomatic: The title crown prince dates from the Han dynasty; under Emperor Ming of Later Han the ceremony of hall audience and investiture prostration first appeared.

sentences.zh: 唐則年長者臨軒冊授，幼者遣使內冊。

translations.literal: Under the Tang, the elder received investiture at the hall; the younger had envoys dispatched for inner investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang, an elder heir received investiture at the hall, while a younger heir was invested inside the palace by dispatched envoys.

sentences.zh: 宋惟用臨軒。

translations.literal: The Song used only hall audience.
translations.idiomatic: The Song used only the hall-audience ceremony.

sentences.zh: 元惟用內冊，不以長幼。

translations.literal: The Yuan used only inner investiture, regardless of age.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan used only inner investiture, without regard to the heir's age.

sentences.zh: 明興，定制，冊皇太子，所司陳設如冊后儀。

translations.literal: When the Ming arose, regulations were fixed: for investing the crown prince, the responsible offices set out arrangements as in the empress-investiture rite.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Ming dynasty regulations were established: for investing the crown prince, the responsible offices arranged the setting as for an empress investiture.

sentences.zh: 設皇太子拜位於丹陛上。

translations.literal: The crown prince's prostration position was set on the red steps.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's obeisance position was set upon the red steps.

sentences.zh: 中嚴，皇帝袞冕御謹身殿，皇太子冕服俟於奉天門。

translations.literal: At the middle vigil, the emperor in full ceremonial robes attended the Hall of Cultivating the Person; the crown prince in coronet and robes waited at the Gate of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: At the middle watch of vigil the emperor in full ceremonial robes took his place in the Hall of Cultivating the Person, while the crown prince in coronet and robes waited at the Gate of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 外辦，皇帝升奉天殿，引禮導皇太子入奉天東門。

translations.literal: When the outer preparations were complete, the emperor ascended the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the usher led the crown prince in through the eastern gate of the Hall of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: When preparations outside were complete, the emperor ascended the Hall of Supreme Harmony and the usher guided the crown prince in through its eastern gate.

sentences.zh: 樂作，由東階升至丹陛位，樂止。

translations.literal: Music began; he ascended by the eastern steps to the position on the red steps; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Music began; he ascended the eastern steps to his place on the red steps; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 百官各就丹墀位。

translations.literal: The hundred officials each took their positions on the red courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Officials each took their places on the red courtyard.

sentences.zh: 樂作，皇太子再拜，興，樂止。

translations.literal: Music began; the crown prince performed two prostrations and rose; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Music began; the crown prince performed two prostrations and rose; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 承制官由殿中門出，立於門外，曰：「有制」。

translations.literal: The edict receiver went out through the central gate of the hall, stood outside the gate, and said, "There is an edict."
translations.idiomatic: The edict receiver emerged through the hall's central gate, stood outside, and announced, "By imperial command."

sentences.zh: 皇太子跪。

translations.literal: The crown prince knelt.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince knelt.

sentences.zh: 宣制曰： 「冊長子某爲皇太子。

translations.literal: The proclamation said: "Invest the eldest son So-and-so as crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: The proclamation ran: "The eldest son So-and-so is invested as crown prince."

sentences.zh: 」皇太子俯伏，興，樂作。

translations.literal: " The crown prince bowed low, rose; music began.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince bowed low to the ground and rose as music began.

sentences.zh: 再拜。

translations.literal: He performed two prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: He performed two more prostrations.

sentences.zh: 樂止。

translations.literal: Music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The music stopped.

sentences.zh: 引禮導皇太子由殿東門入，樂作。

translations.literal: The usher led the crown prince in through the eastern gate of the hall; music began.
translations.idiomatic: The usher guided the crown prince in through the hall's eastern gate as music began.

sentences.zh: 內贊導至御座前，樂止。

translations.literal: The inner announcer guided him before the imperial throne; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The inner announcer guided him before the imperial throne; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 內贊贊跪，贊宣冊。

translations.literal: The inner announcer called to kneel and called to proclaim the commission.
translations.idiomatic: The inner announcer called for him to kneel and for the commission to be read aloud.

sentences.zh: 宣畢，贊搢圭，贊授冊。

translations.literal: When the proclamation was finished, he called to insert the scepter and called to confer the commission.
translations.idiomatic: When the reading was finished, he called for the scepter to be tucked in and for the commission to be conferred.

sentences.zh: 皇太子搢圭，跪受冊，以授內侍。

translations.literal: The crown prince inserted the scepter, knelt to receive the commission, and handed it to an inner attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince tucked in his scepter, knelt to receive the commission, and passed it to an inner attendant.

sentences.zh: 復贊授寶，如授冊儀。

translations.literal: Again he called to confer the seal, as in the commission-conferring rite.
translations.idiomatic: He again called for the seal to be conferred, following the same procedure as for the commission.

sentences.zh: 贊出圭，皇太子出圭，俯伏，興，由殿東門出。

translations.literal: He called to remove the scepter; the crown prince removed the scepter, bowed low, rose, and went out through the eastern gate of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: He called for the scepter to be removed; the crown prince removed it, bowed low, rose, and left through the hall's eastern gate.

sentences.zh: 執事官舉節冊寶隨出。

translations.literal: Officiating officials raised the tally, commission, and seal and followed out.
translations.idiomatic: Officiating officials bore the tally, commission, and seal and followed him out.

sentences.zh: 皇太子復位，樂作。

translations.literal: The crown prince returned to his position; music began.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince returned to his place as music began.

sentences.zh: 四拜興，樂止。

translations.literal: Four prostrations and rising; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He performed four prostrations and rose; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 由東階降，樂作。

translations.literal: He descended by the eastern steps; music began.
translations.idiomatic: He descended the eastern steps as music began.

sentences.zh: 至奉天門，樂止。

translations.literal: He reached the Gate of Supreme Harmony; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the Gate of Supreme Harmony; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 儀仗、鼓樂迎冊寶至文華殿，持節官持節覆命，禮部官奉詔書赴午門開讀，百官迎詔至中書省，頒行。

translations.literal: Guards of honor and drums and music welcomed the commission and seal to the Hall of Literary Glory; the tally-holder held the tally and reported completion; Ministry of Rites officials presented the edict at the Meridian Gate for public reading; the hundred officials welcomed the edict to the Secretariat and promulgated it.
translations.idiomatic: Guards of honor and ceremonial music escorted the commission and seal to the Hall of Literary Glory; the tally-bearer reported back; Ministry of Rites officials presented the edict at the Meridian Gate for public reading; officials received the edict at the Secretariat and promulgated it.

sentences.zh: 侍儀奏禮畢，駕興，還宮。

translations.literal: The ceremonial attendant memorialized that the rite was complete; the imperial carriage rose; they returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial attendant announced that the rite was complete; the emperor's carriage departed; and the court returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 皇太子詣內殿，候皇后升座，行朝謝禮，四拜，恭謝曰：「小子某，茲受冊命，謹詣母后殿下恭謝。

translations.literal: The crown prince went to the inner hall, waited for the empress to ascend the throne, performed the court thanksgiving rite with four prostrations, and respectfully thanked her, saying: "Your son So-and-so, having now received the commission, respectfully comes before Your Majesty the Empress to offer thanks."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince went to the inner hall and waited for the empress to take her seat; he then performed the court thanksgiving rite with four prostrations and said: "Your son So-and-so, having received this commission, respectfully comes before Your Majesty to offer his thanks."

sentences.zh: 」復四拜，禮畢。

translations.literal: " He again performed four prostrations; the rite was complete.
translations.idiomatic: He performed four more prostrations, and the ceremony was finished.

sentences.zh: 親王、世子、郡王俟於文華殿陛上。

translations.literal: Princes, heir apparents of princely houses, and commandery princes waited on the steps of the Hall of Literary Glory.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, princely heirs, and commandery princes waited on the steps of the Hall of Literary Glory.

sentences.zh: 皇太子升座，親王以下由東陛升，就拜位四拜。

translations.literal: The crown prince ascended the throne; princes and those below ascended by the eastern steps, took their prostration positions, and performed four prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince took his seat; princes and those of lower rank ascended the eastern steps, took their places, and performed four prostrations.

sentences.zh: 長王恭賀曰：「小弟某，茲遇長兄皇太子榮膺冊寶，不勝欣忭之至，謹率諸弟詣殿下稱賀。

translations.literal: The eldest prince respectfully congratulated him, saying: "Your younger brother So-and-so, encountering that the eldest brother the crown prince has honorably received the commission and seal, cannot contain his joy and respectfully leads his younger brothers to Your Highness to offer congratulations."
translations.idiomatic: The eldest prince respectfully said: "Your younger brother So-and-so, on learning that our eldest brother the crown prince has received the commission and seal, is overcome with joy and respectfully leads his younger brothers to Your Highness to offer congratulations."

sentences.zh: 」賀畢，皆四拜。

translations.literal: " When congratulations were finished, all performed four prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: When the congratulations were finished, all performed four prostrations.

sentences.zh: 皇太子興，以次出。

translations.literal: The crown prince rose; they departed in order.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince rose, and they withdrew in turn.

sentences.zh: 諸王詣中宮四拜，長王致詞賀畢，皆四拜出。

translations.literal: The princes went to the central palace and performed four prostrations; the eldest prince delivered the congratulatory address; when finished, all performed four prostrations and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The princes went to the central palace and performed four prostrations; the eldest prince delivered the congratulatory address; when finished, all performed four prostrations and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是日，皇太子詣武英殿見諸叔，行家人禮，四拜，諸叔西向坐受。

translations.literal: That day, the crown prince went to the Hall of Martial Glory to see his uncles and performed family rites with four prostrations; the uncles sat facing west to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: That day the crown prince went to the Hall of Martial Glory to see his uncles and performed family obeisance with four prostrations; the uncles sat facing west to receive him.

sentences.zh: 見諸兄，行家人禮，二拜，諸兄西向立受。

translations.literal: He saw his elder brothers and performed family rites with two prostrations; the elder brothers stood facing west to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: He saw his elder brothers and performed family obeisance with two prostrations; the elder brothers stood facing west to receive him.

sentences.zh: 次日，百官進表箋慶賀，內外命婦慶賀中宮，如常儀。

translations.literal: On the following day, the hundred officials submitted memorials and petitions of congratulation; inner and outer titled ladies congratulated the central palace, as in the usual rite.
translations.idiomatic: The next day officials submitted congratulatory memorials and petitions, and titled ladies of the inner and outer courts congratulated the central palace according to the usual ceremony.

sentences.zh: 乃擇日，太子謁太廟。

translations.literal: Then a day was chosen, and the crown prince paid reverent visit to the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: A day was then chosen for the crown prince to pay reverent visit to the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十八年，皇太子、親王俱授金冊，不用寶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Hongwu, the crown prince and princes were all conferred gold commissions, without using a seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year of Hongwu the crown prince and princes all received gold commission documents, without an imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年定，先三日齋戒，遣官祭告天地、宗廟，受冊寶畢，先詣太廟謁告，後至奉天殿謝恩，乃入謝中宮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle it was fixed: three days beforehand there was fasting; officials were dispatched to offer sacrifices and announce to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temples; when reception of the commission and seal was finished, they first went to the Grand Ancestral Temple for reverent announcement, afterward came to the Hall of Supreme Harmony for thanksgiving, and then entered to thank the central palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongle it was established that three days of fasting preceded the ceremony, with officials dispatched to announce the event to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples; after receiving the commission and seal, the crown prince first visited the Grand Ancestral Temple, then went to the Hall of Supreme Harmony to offer thanks, and finally entered the central palace to thank the empress.

sentences.zh: 二十二年十月，冊東宮，以梓宮在殯，樂設而不作。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twenty-second year, when the Eastern Palace was invested, because the coffin of the deceased emperor was in mourning display, music was set up but not played.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twenty-second year, when the Eastern Palace heir was invested, the late emperor's coffin still lay in state, so music was posted but not played.

sentences.zh: 奉先殿行禮畢，仍詣几筵謁告。

translations.literal: When the rite at the Hall of Imperial Ancestors was finished, they still went to the spirit table to pay reverent announcement.
translations.idiomatic: After the ceremony at the Hall of Imperial Ancestors was finished, they still paid reverent visit at the spirit table.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年十一月，皇子生，羣臣表請立太子，三年二月行禮，以太子尚幼，乃命正、副使授冊寶於文華門。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Xuande a prince was born; the officials memorialized requesting establishment of the crown prince; in the second month of the third year the rite was performed; because the crown prince was still young, the chief and deputy envoys were ordered to confer the commission and seal at the Gate of Literary Glory.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year of Xuande a prince was born and officials memorialized to have him named heir; the ceremony was performed in the second month of the third year, but because the heir was still young the chief and deputy envoys were ordered to confer the commission and seal at the Gate of Literary Glory.

sentences.zh: 成化十一年以冊立皇太子禮成，文武官分五等，賜綵緞有差。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Chenghua, when the rite of investing the crown prince was completed, civil and military officials were divided into five grades and bestowed colored silks in differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Chenghua, when the crown prince investiture was completed, civil and military officials were divided into five grades and rewarded with colored silks in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十八年二，月冊東宮，帝詣南郊告上帝，詣太廟告皇祖，自北郊及列聖宗廟以下皆遣官。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighteenth year of Jiajing, when the Eastern Palace was invested, the emperor went to the southern suburb to announce to the Supreme Lord, went to the Grand Ancestral Temple to announce to the imperial ancestor, and from the northern suburb and the temples of successive sage emperors downward all dispatched officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighteenth year of Jiajing, when the Eastern Palace heir was invested, the emperor announced the event to the Supreme Lord at the southern suburb and to the imperial ancestor at the Grand Ancestral Temple, while officials were dispatched for announcements from the northern suburb and the temples of successive emperors downward.

sentences.zh: 時太子方二歲，保姆奉之，迎冊寶於文華殿門，詣皇帝前謝恩，皇后、貴妃代太子八拜。

translations.literal: At that time the crown prince was only two years old; the nurse held him; they welcomed the commission and seal at the gate of the Hall of Literary Glory; they went before the emperor to offer thanks; the empress and honored consort performed eight prostrations on the crown prince's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was then only two years old; a nurse held him as the commission and seal were received at the gate of the Hall of Literary Glory; the empress and honored consort performed eight prostrations before the emperor on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 詣皇后前，貴妃代八拜。

translations.literal: Before the empress, the honored consort performed eight prostrations on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Before the empress, the honored consort again performed eight prostrations on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 詣貴妃前，保姆代四拜。

translations.literal: Before the honored consort, the nurse performed four prostrations on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Before the honored consort, the nurse performed four prostrations on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 餘如常儀。

translations.literal: The rest followed the usual rite.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder followed the usual ceremony.

sentences.zh: 其皇太子妃受冊，與皇太子同日傳制。

translations.literal: As for the crown princess receiving the commission, the edict was transmitted on the same day as the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The crown princess received her commission on the same day, with the edict transmitted together with the crown prince's.

sentences.zh: 節冊將至內殿，妃降自東階，迎置於案。

translations.literal: When the tally and commission were about to reach the inner hall, the princess descended by the eastern steps, welcomed them, and placed them on the table.
translations.idiomatic: As the tally and commission approached the inner hall, the princess descended the eastern steps to receive them and set them upon the table.

sentences.zh: 贊就拜位，贊跪，妃跪。

translations.literal: The announcer called to take the prostration position; called to kneel; the princess knelt.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer directed her to the obeisance position, called for her to kneel, and she knelt.

sentences.zh: 贊宣冊，女官跪取冊，立宣畢。

translations.literal: The announcer called to proclaim the commission; a female official knelt, took the commission, stood, and finished proclaiming it.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer called for the commission to be read; a female official knelt, took the document, rose, and read it aloud to the end.

sentences.zh: 贊授冊，贊搢圭。

translations.literal: The announcer called to confer the commission and called to insert the scepter.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer called for the commission to be conferred and for the scepter to be tucked in.

sentences.zh: 女官以冊授妃，妃搢圭，受冊訖，以授女官。

translations.literal: The female official handed the commission to the princess; the princess inserted the scepter; when she had received the commission, she handed it to the female official.
translations.idiomatic: A female official handed the commission to the princess; she tucked in her scepter, received the document, and passed it back to the female official.

sentences.zh: 女官跪受，捧立。

translations.literal: The female official knelt to receive it and stood holding it.
translations.idiomatic: The female official knelt to receive it and stood holding it aloft.

sentences.zh: 贊出圭，興，四拜。

translations.literal: The announcer called to remove the scepter; she rose and performed four prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer called for the scepter to be removed; she rose and performed four prostrations.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，內官持節出，妃送至殿外，正副使持節覆命。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, an inner official held the tally and went out; the princess escorted them to outside the hall; the chief and deputy envoys held the tally and reported completion.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony was finished, an inner official bore the tally out; the princess escorted the envoys to the hall's entrance; and the chief and deputy envoys returned the tally and reported back.

sentences.zh: 是日，妃具禮服詣奉先殿行謁告禮。

translations.literal: That day, the princess in full ceremonial dress went to the Hall of Imperial Ancestors to perform the reverent announcement rite.
translations.idiomatic: That day the princess, in full ceremonial dress, paid a reverent visit of announcement at the Hall of Imperial Ancestors.

sentences.zh: 隨詣宮門，俟皇帝、皇后升座，入謝恩，行八拜禮。

translations.literal: Then she went to the palace gate, waited for the emperor and empress to ascend the throne, entered to offer thanks, and performed the eight-prostration rite.
translations.idiomatic: She then went to the palace gate, waited for the emperor and empress to take their seats, entered to offer thanks, and performed eight prostrations.

sentences.zh: 又詣各宮皇妃前，行四拜禮。

translations.literal: Again she went before the honored imperial consorts of each palace and performed the four-prostration rite.
translations.idiomatic: She then went before the honored imperial consorts of each palace and performed four prostrations.

sentences.zh: 還宮，詣皇太子前，亦四拜。

translations.literal: Returning to the palace, she went before the crown prince and likewise performed four prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: She then returned to the palace and, before the crown prince, performed four prostrations as well.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，升座，王妃、公主、郡主及外命婦，于丹墀拜賀如儀。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, she ascended the seat; princess consorts, princesses, commandery princesses, and external titled ladies offered congratulatory bows in the red courtyard as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony was finished, she took her seat; princess consorts, princesses, commandery princesses, and external titled ladies offered congratulatory bows in the courtyard according to the prescribed rite.

sentences.zh: 冊親王及王妃儀

translations.literal: Rites for investing princes and princess consorts
translations.idiomatic: Investing Princes and Princess Consorts

sentences.zh: 漢冊親王於廟。

translations.literal: Under the Han, princes were invested at the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, princes were invested at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 唐臨軒冊命，禮極詳備。

translations.literal: Under the Tang, investiture was conferred at hall audience; the rites were extremely detailed and complete.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang, princes received investiture at hall audience in rites of the utmost detail and completeness.

sentences.zh: 宋有冊命之文，皆上表辭免，惟迎官誥還第。

translations.literal: The Song had investiture texts; all submitted memorials declining acceptance, and only welcomed the officials bearing the patent and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The Song issued investiture documents, but recipients always memorialized to decline; they merely received the officials bearing the patent and returned to their residences.

sentences.zh: 元亦降制命之，不行冊禮。

translations.literal: The Yuan also issued command-investitures and did not perform the investiture rite.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan likewise issued command-investitures and did not perform the formal investiture ceremony.

sentences.zh: 明洪武三年定制，冊命親王，先期告宗廟，所司陳設如冊東宮儀。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu the Ming established regulations: to invest princes, beforehand they announced to the ancestral temple; the responsible offices set out arrangements as in the Eastern Palace investiture rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongwu the Ming established regulations for investing princes: the ancestral temple was notified in advance, and the responsible offices arranged the setting according to the Eastern Palace investiture ceremony.

sentences.zh: 至日，皇帝御奉天殿，皇太子、親王由奉天東門入。

translations.literal: On the appointed day, the emperor attended the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the crown prince and princes entered through the eastern gate of the Hall of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day the emperor took his place in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, and the crown prince and princes entered through its eastern gate.

sentences.zh: 樂作，升自東陛。

translations.literal: Music began; they ascended by the eastern steps.
translations.idiomatic: Music began as they ascended the eastern steps.

sentences.zh: 皇太子由殿東門入，內贊導至御前，侍立位。

translations.literal: The crown prince entered through the hall's eastern gate; the inner announcer led him to before the throne to the attendant standing position.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince entered through the hall's eastern gate; the inner announcer guided him to the attendant position before the throne.

sentences.zh: 親王入至丹陛拜位，樂止。

translations.literal: The princes entered to the prostration position on the red steps; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The princes entered to the obeisance position on the red steps, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 贊拜，樂作。

translations.literal: The announcer called for prostration; music began.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer called for obeisance as music began.

sentences.zh: 再拜，興，樂止。

translations.literal: Second prostration; they rose; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: They performed a second prostration, then rose; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 承制官承制如儀，諸王皆跪，宣制曰：「封皇子某爲某王，某爲某王。

translations.literal: The edict proclaimer received the edict as prescribed; all princes knelt; he proclaimed the edict, saying: "I enfeoff Imperial Son So-and-so as Prince of Such-and-such, and So-and-so as Prince of Such-and-such."
translations.idiomatic: The edict proclaimer received the imperial command as prescribed; all princes knelt as he proclaimed: "Imperial Son So-and-so is enfeoffed as Prince of Such-and-such, and So-and-so as Prince of Such-and-such."

sentences.zh: 」宣畢，諸王俯伏，興。

translations.literal: " When the proclamation was finished, all princes bowed low; they rose.
translations.idiomatic: When the proclamation was finished, all princes bowed low and then rose.

sentences.zh: 贊拜，樂作。

translations.literal: The announcer called for prostration; music began.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer called for obeisance as music began.

sentences.zh: 再拜，興，樂止。

translations.literal: Second prostration; they rose; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: They performed a second prostration, then rose; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 引禮導王由殿東外入，樂作。

translations.literal: The usher led the prince in through the eastern outer entrance of the hall; music began.
translations.idiomatic: The usher guided the prince in through the hall's outer eastern entrance as music began.

sentences.zh: 內贊引至御座前拜位，樂止。

translations.literal: The inner announcer led him to the prostration position before the imperial throne; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The inner announcer guided him to the obeisance position before the throne, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 王跪。

translations.literal: The prince knelt.
translations.idiomatic: The prince knelt.

sentences.zh: 贊授冊，捧冊官以冊授讀冊官，讀訖，以授丞相。

translations.literal: The announcer called to confer the commission; the bearer of the commission handed it to the reader of the commission; when the reading was finished, he handed it to the chief counsellor.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer called for the commission to be conferred; the bearer handed the document to the reader, and when the reading was finished it was passed to the chief counsellor.

sentences.zh: 丞相授王，王搢圭受，以授內使。

translations.literal: The chief counsellor handed it to the prince; the prince inserted his scepter and received it, then handed it to the inner attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The chief counsellor handed the commission to the prince; the prince tucked in his scepter, received it, and passed it to an inner attendant.

sentences.zh: 授寶如上儀。

translations.literal: Conferring the seal followed the above rite.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial seal was conferred according to the procedure above.

sentences.zh: 訖，王出圭，俯伏，興。

translations.literal: When finished, the prince removed his scepter, bowed low, and rose.
translations.idiomatic: When this was finished, the prince removed his scepter, bowed low, and rose.

sentences.zh: 引禮導王出，復位。

translations.literal: The usher led the prince out and he returned to his position.
translations.idiomatic: The usher guided the prince out, and he returned to his place.

sentences.zh: 以次引諸王入殿，授冊寶如儀。

translations.literal: In order, each prince was led into the hall and received commission and seal as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: Each prince was then led into the hall in turn and received the commission and seal according to the prescribed ceremony.

sentences.zh: 內使以冊寶置彩亭訖，贊拜，樂作。

translations.literal: When the inner attendants had placed the commission and seal in the ceremonial canopy, the announcer called for prostration; music began.
translations.idiomatic: After inner attendants placed the commission and seal in the ceremonial canopy, the announcer called for obeisance as music began.

sentences.zh: 諸王皆四拜，興，樂止。

translations.literal: All princes performed four prostrations, rose; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: All princes performed four prostrations, then rose; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 內使舉亭前行，親王由東階降，樂作。

translations.literal: Inner attendants raised the canopy and proceeded forward; princes descended by the eastern steps; music began.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants raised the canopy and moved forward as the princes descended the eastern steps to music.

sentences.zh: 出奉天東門，樂止。

translations.literal: They went out through the eastern gate of the Hall of Supreme Harmony; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: They passed out through the eastern gate of the Hall of Supreme Harmony, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書請詔書用寶，赴午門開讀。

translations.literal: The Minister of Rites requested the edict be sealed and presented at the Meridian Gate for public reading.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Rites requested that the edict be sealed and presented at the Meridian Gate for public reading.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，皇帝還宮，皇太子出。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, the emperor returned to the palace and the crown prince departed.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony was finished, the emperor returned to the palace and the crown prince withdrew.

sentences.zh: 王年幼，則遣官齎冊寶授之。

translations.literal: If a prince was young, officials were dispatched to carry the commission and seal and confer them on him.
translations.idiomatic: If a prince was still young, officials were dispatched to carry the commission and seal and confer them upon him.

sentences.zh: 丞相承制至王所，東北立，西南向，宣制。

translations.literal: The chief counsellor received the edict and went to the prince's residence, standing at the northeast facing southwest, and proclaimed the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The chief counsellor received the imperial command and went to the prince's residence, standing at the northeast and facing southwest to proclaim the edict.

sentences.zh: 最幼者行保抱之禮。

translations.literal: The youngest performed the rite of being held and carried.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest prince received the rite of being held in arms.

sentences.zh: 是日，親王朝謝皇后、太子，與東宮受冊朝謝同。

translations.literal: That day, princes paid court thanks to the empress and crown prince, the same as when the Eastern Palace received investiture.
translations.idiomatic: That day the princes paid court thanks to the empress and crown prince, following the same procedure as when the Eastern Palace heir received investiture.

sentences.zh: 親王各自行賀，幼者詣長者，行四拜禮。

translations.literal: Each prince offered congratulations on his own; the younger went to the elder and performed the four-prostration rite.
translations.idiomatic: Each prince offered congratulations in turn; younger princes went before their elders and performed four prostrations.

sentences.zh: 百官詣親王賀，亦行四拜禮。

translations.literal: The hundred officials went to congratulate the princes, also performing the four-prostration rite.
translations.idiomatic: Officials went to congratulate the princes, likewise performing four prostrations.

sentences.zh: 丞相至殿上跪，文武官於庭中。

translations.literal: The chief counsellor knelt on the hall; civil and military officials were in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The chief counsellor knelt on the hall while civil and military officials stood in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 丞相致詞曰：「某官某等，茲遇親王殿下榮膺冊寶，封建禮成，無任欣忭之至。

translations.literal: The chief counsellor delivered the congratulatory address: "We officials So-and-so and others, on this occasion of Your Highness the Prince receiving commission and seal and completion of enfeoffment, cannot contain our utmost joy."
translations.idiomatic: The chief counsellor delivered the congratulatory address: "We, So-and-so and the other officials, on this occasion of Your Highness receiving the commission and seal and completing your enfeoffment, are filled with inexpressible joy."
