sentences.zh: 」賀畢，丞相及百官復四拜。

translations.literal: " When congratulations were finished, the chief counsellor and the hundred officials again performed four prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: When congratulations were finished, the chief counsellor and all officials again performed four prostrations.

sentences.zh: 次日，皇太子冕服於奉天殿朝賀皇帝，太子致詞曰：「長子某，茲遇諸弟某等受封建國，謹詣父皇陛下稱賀。

translations.literal: The next day, the crown prince in coronet and robes at the Hall of Supreme Harmony paid court congratulations to the emperor; the crown prince delivered the address: "Your eldest son So-and-so, on this occasion of my brothers So-and-so and others receiving enfeoffment and establishment of their states, respectfully come before Your Majesty the Emperor to offer congratulations."
translations.idiomatic: The next day the crown prince, in full regalia, paid court congratulations to the emperor in the Hall of Supreme Harmony and said: "Your eldest son So-and-so, on this occasion of my brothers So-and-so and others receiving enfeoffment and establishment of their domains, respectfully come before Your Majesty to offer congratulations."

sentences.zh: 」賀中宮，致詞曰：「謹詣母后殿下稱賀。

translations.literal: " Congratulating the central palace, he delivered the address: "Respectfully come before Your Majesty the Empress to offer congratulations."
translations.idiomatic: Congratulating the empress, he said: "I respectfully come before Your Majesty to offer congratulations."

sentences.zh: 」百官進表箋賀皇帝及中宮、東宮，如東宮受冊儀。

translations.literal: " The hundred officials submitted memorials and congratulatory documents to congratulate the emperor, the central palace, and the Eastern Palace, as in the Eastern Palace investiture rite.
translations.idiomatic: Officials submitted memorials and congratulatory documents to the emperor, the empress, and the Eastern Palace, following the Eastern Palace investiture ceremony.

sentences.zh: 內外命婦賀中宮，致詞曰：「妾某氏等，茲遇親王受封建國，恭詣皇后殿下稱賀。

translations.literal: Internal and external titled ladies congratulated the central palace, delivering the address: "We, Lady So-and-so and others, on this occasion of princes receiving enfeoffment and establishment of states, respectfully come before Her Majesty the Empress to offer congratulations."
translations.idiomatic: Internal and external titled ladies congratulated the empress, saying: "We, Lady So-and-so and the others, on this occasion of princes receiving enfeoffment and establishment of their domains, respectfully come before Her Majesty to offer congratulations."

sentences.zh: 」是日，百官及命婦各賜宴。

translations.literal: " That day, the hundred officials and titled ladies were each given banquets.
translations.idiomatic: That day banquets were bestowed upon officials and titled ladies alike.

sentences.zh: 擇日，諸王謁太廟。

translations.literal: A day was chosen for all princes to pay reverent visit to the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: A day was chosen for all princes to pay reverent visit at the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 時秦、晉、燕、楚、吳五王皆長，而齊、潭、趙、魯四王方幼，故兼具其制。

translations.literal: At that time the five princes of Qin, Jin, Yan, Chu, and Wu were all grown, while the four princes of Qi, Tan, Zhao, and Lu were still young; therefore both procedures were combined.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Princes of Qin, Jin, Yan, Chu, and Wu were all grown, while the Princes of Qi, Tan, Zhao, and Lu were still young; the regulations therefore combined both procedures.

sentences.zh: 靖江王則以親王封，故視秦、晉儀。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jingjiang was enfeoffed as a full prince, so he followed the rites of Qin and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jingjiang was enfeoffed with full princely rank and therefore followed the ceremony used for the Princes of Qin and Jin.

sentences.zh: 二十八年定制，親王嫡長子，年十歲，授金冊寶，立爲王世子。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year regulations were established: a prince's eldest legitimate son, at age ten, received the gold commission and seal and was installed as heir prince of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations established in the twenty-eighth year provided that a prince's eldest legitimate son, at age ten, received the gold commission and seal and was installed as heir prince of the princely domain.

sentences.zh: 次嫡及庶子皆封郡王。

translations.literal: Second legitimate sons and all sons of concubines were enfeoffed as commandery princes.
translations.idiomatic: Second sons by the principal consort and all sons of concubines were enfeoffed as commandery princes.

sentences.zh: 凡王世子必以嫡長，王年三十，正妃未有嫡子，其子止爲郡王。

translations.literal: In all cases the heir prince of the state must be the eldest legitimate son; if when the prince was thirty the principal consort still had no legitimate son, his son could only be a commandery prince.
translations.idiomatic: The heir prince of a princely domain had to be the eldest legitimate son; if at age thirty the prince's principal consort still had no legitimate son, any son born to her could only be enfeoffed as a commandery prince.

sentences.zh: 待王與正妃年五十無嫡子，始立庶長子爲王世子，襲封。

translations.literal: Only when prince and principal consort reached fifty with no legitimate son was the eldest son of a concubine first installed as heir prince of the state to inherit the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the prince and principal consort reached fifty without a legitimate son was the eldest son of a concubine installed as heir prince to inherit the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣人行冊命之禮。

translations.literal: The court dispatched officials to perform the commission-investiture rite.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched officials to perform the commission-investiture ceremony.

sentences.zh: 成化末，封興、岐、益、衡、雍五王，帝親告奉先殿，遣使就各王府冊之，罷臨軒禮。

translations.literal: At the end of Chenghua, when the five princes Xing, Qi, Yi, Heng, and Yong were enfeoffed, the emperor personally announced at the Hall of Imperial Ancestors and dispatched envoys to each prince's residence to invest them, abolishing the hall-audience rite.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Chenghua reign, when the Princes of Xing, Qi, Yi, Heng, and Yong were enfeoffed, the emperor personally announced the event at the Hall of Imperial Ancestors and dispatched envoys to invest each prince at his residence, abolishing the hall-audience ceremony.

sentences.zh: 而諸王當襲封者，俱於歲終遣官冊封。

translations.literal: As for princes due to inherit enfeoffments, all were invested by dispatched officials at year's end.
translations.idiomatic: Princes due to inherit enfeoffments were all invested by dispatched officials at year's end.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，改於孟春，著爲令。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign it was changed to the first month of spring and established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign the timing was changed to early spring and established as regulation.

sentences.zh: 冊王妃與冊太子妃儀同。

translations.literal: Investing a princess consort followed the same rite as investing the crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: Investing a princess consort followed the same ceremony as investing the crown princess.

sentences.zh: 冊公主儀

translations.literal: Rites for investing an imperial princess
translations.idiomatic: Investing Imperial Princesses

sentences.zh: 洪武九年七月，命使冊公主。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the ninth year of Hongwu, envoys were ordered to invest an imperial princess.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the ninth year of Hongwu, envoys were ordered to invest an imperial princess.

sentences.zh: 設冊案於清乾宮御座之東南，冊用銀字鍍金。

translations.literal: A commission table was set southeast of the imperial throne in the Palace of Pure Qi; the commission used silver characters plated with gold.
translations.idiomatic: A table for the commission document was placed southeast of the throne in the Palace of Pure Qi; the commission itself bore silver characters plated with gold.

sentences.zh: 皇帝、皇后升御座，遣使捧冊傳制如儀。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress ascended the throne; envoys were dispatched to hold the commission and transmit the edict as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress took their seats and dispatched envoys to bear the commission and transmit the imperial command according to the prescribed ceremony.

sentences.zh: 使者至華蓋殿，公主拜受，其儀略與冊太子妃同。

translations.literal: When the envoys reached the Hall of Flowering Canopy, the princess bowed to receive it; the rite was generally the same as investing the crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys reached the Hall of Flowering Canopy, the princess bowed to receive the commission; the ceremony was largely the same as that for investing the crown princess.

sentences.zh: 凡皇姑曰大長公主，皇姊妹曰長公主，皇女曰公主，親王女曰郡主，郡王女曰縣主，孫女曰郡君，曾孫女曰縣君，玄孫女曰鄉君。

translations.literal: In general the emperor's paternal aunts were called Grand Senior Princesses, paternal sisters Senior Princesses, daughters Princesses, princes' daughters Commandery Princesses, commandery princes' daughters County Princesses, granddaughters Commandery Ladies, great-granddaughters County Ladies, and great-great-granddaughters Township Ladies.
translations.idiomatic: In general, the emperor's paternal aunts were styled Grand Senior Princesses; his sisters, Senior Princesses; his daughters, Princesses; princes' daughters, Commandery Princesses; commandery princes' daughters, County Princesses; granddaughters, Commandery Ladies; great-granddaughters, County Ladies; and great-great-granddaughters, Township Ladies.

sentences.zh: 郡主以下，受誥封，不冊命。

translations.literal: Below commandery princess rank, they received patent enfeoffment and were not invested by commission.
translations.idiomatic: Those below the rank of commandery princess received patent enfeoffment rather than formal commission investiture.

sentences.zh: 皇帝加元服儀

translations.literal: Rites for the emperor's capping investiture
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's Coming-of-Age Ceremony

sentences.zh: 古者冠必於廟，天子四加。

translations.literal: In antiquity capping had to be at the temple; the Son of Heaven received four investitures.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the capping ceremony had to be performed at the temple, and the Son of Heaven received four investitures.

sentences.zh: 魏以後始冠於正殿，又以天子至尊，禮惟一加，歷代因之。

translations.literal: From Wei onward capping began in the main hall; because the Son of Heaven was supreme, the rite had only one investiture, and successive dynasties followed this.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wei dynasty onward capping was performed in the main hall; because the Son of Heaven stood supreme, the rite was reduced to a single investiture, and successive dynasties followed this practice.

sentences.zh: 明洪武三年定制。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu the Ming established regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations were established in the third year of Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 先期，太史院卜日，工部制冕服，翰林院撰祝文，禮部具儀注。

translations.literal: Beforehand, the Directorate of Astronomy divined the day; the Ministry of Works made coronet and robes; the Hanlin Academy drafted the prayer text; the Ministry of Rites prepared the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand the Directorate of Astronomy divined the auspicious day, the Ministry of Works made the coronet and robes, the Hanlin Academy drafted the prayer text, and the Ministry of Rites prepared the ceremonial regulations.

sentences.zh: 中書省承制，命某官攝太師，某官攝太尉。

translations.literal: The Secretariat received the edict and appointed such-and-such official to act as Grand Preceptor and such-and-such official to act as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat received the imperial command and appointed such-and-such official to serve as acting Grand Preceptor and such-and-such official as acting Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 既卜日，遣官告天地、宗廟。

translations.literal: Once the day was divined, officials were dispatched to announce to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Once the day was chosen, officials were dispatched to announce the event to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 前一日，內使監令陳御冠席於奉天殿正中，其南設冕服案及香案寶案。

translations.literal: The day before, the director of inner attendants ordered the imperial capping mat set in the center of the Hall of Supreme Harmony; south of it were set tables for coronet and robes, incense, and the seal.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the ceremony, the director of inner attendants had the imperial capping mat placed in the center of the Hall of Supreme Harmony, with tables for the coronet and robes, incense, and the seal set to the south.

sentences.zh: 侍儀司設太師、太尉起居位於文樓南，西向，設拜位於丹墀內道，設侍立位於殿上御席西，設盥洗位於丹陛西。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Ceremonial Attendants set standing positions for Grand Preceptor and Grand Commandant south of the Literary Tower facing west, prostration positions on the inner path of the red courtyard, attendant positions west of the imperial mat on the hall, and ablution positions west of the red steps.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Ceremonial Attendants placed standing positions for the Grand Preceptor and Grand Commandant south of the Literary Tower, facing west; obeisance positions on the inner path of the red courtyard; attendant positions west of the imperial mat on the hall; and ablution positions west of the red steps.

sentences.zh: 其百官及諸執事位次如大朝儀。

translations.literal: The positions of the hundred officials and various functionaries followed the grand audience rite.
translations.idiomatic: The positions of officials and various functionaries followed the grand audience ceremony.

sentences.zh: 是日質明，鼓三嚴，百官入。

translations.literal: At dawn that day, the drum sounded three rounds of vigil; the hundred officials entered.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn that day, after the triple drum signal marking the third watch of vigil, officials entered.

sentences.zh: 皇帝服空頂幘、雙童髻、雙玉導、絳紗袍，御輿以出。

translations.literal: The emperor wore an open-topped headcloth, double child topknots, double jade hairpins, and a crimson gauze robe, and went out in the imperial palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore an open-topped headcloth, double child topknots, double jade hairpins, and a crimson gauze robe, and went out in the imperial palanquin.

sentences.zh: 侍衛警蹕奏如儀。

translations.literal: Guards cleared the way and reported as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: Guards cleared the way and reported according to the prescribed ceremony.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升座。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 鳴鞭報時訖，通班贊各供事。

translations.literal: When the whip was cracked and the time reported, the relay announcer called each to take up his duty.
translations.idiomatic: After the whip was cracked and the hour reported, the relay announcer called each official to take up his duty.

sentences.zh: 太師太尉先入，就拜位，百官皆入。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor and Grand Commandant entered first and took their prostration positions; all officials entered.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor and Grand Commandant entered first and took their obeisance positions; then all officials entered.

sentences.zh: 贊拜，樂作。

translations.literal: The announcer called for prostration; music began.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer called for obeisance as music began.

sentences.zh: 四拜，興，樂止。

translations.literal: Four prostrations; they rose; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: They performed four prostrations, then rose; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 引禮導太師先詣盥洗位，搢笏盥帨訖，出笏，由西陛升。

translations.literal: The usher first led the Grand Preceptor to the ablution place; he inserted his tablet, washed and dried his hands; when finished, removed the tablet and ascended by the western steps.
translations.idiomatic: The usher first guided the Grand Preceptor to the ablution place; he inserted his tablet, washed and dried his hands, removed the tablet, and ascended the western steps.

sentences.zh: 內贊接引至御席西，東向立。

translations.literal: The inner announcer led him to west of the imperial mat, standing facing east.
translations.idiomatic: The inner announcer guided him to the west of the imperial mat, where he stood facing east.

sentences.zh: 引禮復導太尉盥搢訖，入立於太師南。

translations.literal: The usher again led the Grand Commandant to wash and insert his tablet; when finished he entered and stood south of the Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The usher then guided the Grand Commandant through ablution and insertion of his tablet; when finished he entered and stood south of the Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 侍儀奏請加元服。

translations.literal: Ceremonial attendants reported requesting the capping investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial attendants reported a request for the capping investiture.

sentences.zh: 太尉詣皇帝前，少右，跪搢笏。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant went before the emperor, slightly to the right, knelt, and inserted his tablet.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant went before the emperor, slightly to the right, knelt, and inserted his tablet.

sentences.zh: 脫空頂幘以授內使，置於箱。

translations.literal: He removed the open-topped headcloth and handed it to the inner attendant, who placed it in a box.
translations.idiomatic: He removed the open-topped headcloth and handed it to an inner attendant, who placed it in a box.

sentences.zh: 進櫛設纚畢，出笏，興，退立於西。

translations.literal: He presented the comb and set the cap strings; when finished, removed the tablet, rose, withdrew, and stood to the west.
translations.idiomatic: He presented the comb and set the cap strings; when finished he removed his tablet, rose, withdrew, and stood to the west.

sentences.zh: 太師前，北向立。

translations.literal: The Grand Preceptor went forward, standing facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor stepped forward and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 內使監令取冕立於左，太師祝曰：「令月吉日，始加元服，壽考維祺，以介景福。

translations.literal: The director of inner attendants took the coronet and stood to the left; the Grand Preceptor intoned the prayer: "On this auspicious day of this month, the first capping investiture begins; may you attain long life and good fortune, and thereby receive great blessing."
translations.idiomatic: The director of inner attendants took the coronet and stood to the left; the Grand Preceptor intoned the prayer: "On this auspicious day of this month, the first capping investiture begins; may you attain long life and good fortune, and thereby receive great blessing."

sentences.zh: 」內使監令捧冕，跪授太師。

translations.literal: " The director of inner attendants held the coronet, knelt, and handed it to the Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The director of inner attendants held the coronet, knelt, and handed it to the Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 太師搢笏，跪受冕。

translations.literal: The Grand Preceptor inserted his tablet, knelt, and received the coronet.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor inserted his tablet, knelt, and received the coronet.

sentences.zh: 加冠、加簪纓訖，出笏，興，退立於西。

translations.literal: When crowning and adding hairpin and tassel were finished, he removed his tablet, rose, withdrew, and stood to the west.
translations.idiomatic: When the crowning and addition of hairpin and tassel were finished, he removed his tablet, rose, withdrew, and stood to the west.

sentences.zh: 御用監令奏請皇帝著袞服，皇帝興，著袞服。

translations.literal: The director of the Imperial Workshop reported requesting the emperor put on sacrificial robes; the emperor rose and put on sacrificial robes.
translations.idiomatic: The director of the Imperial Workshop reported a request for the emperor to put on sacrificial robes; the emperor rose and donned them.

sentences.zh: 侍儀奏請就御座，內贊贊進醴，樂作。

translations.literal: Ceremonial attendants reported requesting him take the imperial seat; the inner announcer called to present the ritual wine; music began.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial attendants reported a request for him to take the imperial seat; the inner announcer called for the ritual wine to be presented as music began.

sentences.zh: 太師詣御前北面立，光祿卿奉酒進授太師，太師搢笏受酒，祝曰：「甘醴惟厚，嘉薦令芳。

translations.literal: The Grand Preceptor went before the throne standing facing north; the Minister of Imperial Entertainments presented wine and handed it to the Grand Preceptor; the Grand Preceptor inserted his tablet and received the wine, intoning the prayer: "Sweet wine indeed is rich; fine offerings are fragrant and good."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor went before the throne and stood facing north; the Minister of Imperial Entertainments presented wine and handed it to him; the Grand Preceptor inserted his tablet, received the wine, and intoned the prayer: "Sweet wine indeed is rich; fine offerings are fragrant and good."

sentences.zh: 承天之休，壽考不忘。

translations.literal: Receiving Heaven's favor, long life unforgotten.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving Heaven's favor, may long life never be forgotten.

sentences.zh: 」祝訖，跪授內使。

translations.literal: " When the prayer was finished, he knelt and handed it to an inner attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the prayer was finished, he knelt and handed the cup to an inner attendant.

sentences.zh: 內使跪受酒，捧進。

translations.literal: The inner attendant knelt to receive the wine and held it forward in presentation.
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendant knelt to receive the wine and bore it forward in presentation.

sentences.zh: 皇帝受，祭少許，啐酒訖，以虛盞授內使，樂止。

translations.literal: The emperor received it, offered a small libation, finished tasting the wine, handed the empty cup to the inner attendant; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received it, offered a small libation, performed the ritual sip, handed the empty cup to the inner attendant, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 內使受盞降，授太師。

translations.literal: The inner attendant received the cup, descended, and handed it to the Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendant received the cup, descended, and passed it to the Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 太師受盞興，以授光祿卿，光祿卿受盞退。

translations.literal: The Grand Preceptor received the cup and rose, handed it to the Minister of Imperial Entertainments; the Minister of Imperial Entertainments received the cup and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor received the cup and rose, then handed it to the Minister of Imperial Entertainments, who received it and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太師出笏，退，復位。

translations.literal: The Grand Preceptor removed his tablet, withdrew, and returned to his position.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor removed his tablet, withdrew, and returned to his place.

sentences.zh: 內贊導太師太尉出殿西門，樂作，降自西階。

translations.literal: The inner announcer guided the Grand Preceptor and Grand Commandant out through the hall's western gate; music began; they descended by the western steps.
translations.idiomatic: The inner announcer guided the Grand Preceptor and Grand Commandant out through the hall's western gate as music began; they descended the western steps.

sentences.zh: 引禮導至丹墀拜位，樂止。

translations.literal: The usher guided them to the prostration position on the red courtyard; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The usher guided them to the obeisance position on the red courtyard, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 贊拜，樂作。

translations.literal: The announcer called for prostration; music began.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer called for obeisance as music began.

sentences.zh: 太師太尉及文武官皆四拜，興，樂止。

translations.literal: The Grand Preceptor, Grand Commandant, and civil and military officials all performed four prostrations and rose; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor, Grand Commandant, and civil and military officials all performed four prostrations and rose; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 三舞蹈，山呼，俯伏，興，樂作。

translations.literal: Three ritual dance prostrations, mountain shout, bowed low, rose; music began.
translations.idiomatic: They performed three ritual dance prostrations and the mountain shout, bowed low, and rose as music began.

sentences.zh: 復四拜，樂止。

translations.literal: Again four prostrations; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: They performed four more prostrations, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，皇帝興，鳴鞭，樂作。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, the emperor rose; the whip was cracked; music began.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony was finished, the emperor rose; the whip was cracked, and music began.

sentences.zh: 入宮，樂止。

translations.literal: He entered the palace; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the palace, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 百官出。

translations.literal: The hundred officials departed.
translations.idiomatic: The officials withdrew.

sentences.zh: 皇帝改服通天冠、絳紗袍，拜謁太后，如正旦儀。

translations.literal: The emperor changed into the Heaven-Penetrating Coronet and crimson gauze robe, paid reverent visit to the Empress Dowager, as in the New Year's Day rite.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor changed into the Heaven-Penetrating Coronet and crimson gauze robe and paid reverent visit to the Empress Dowager according to the New Year's Day ceremony.

sentences.zh: 擇日謁太廟，與時祭同。

translations.literal: A day was chosen to visit the Grand Ancestral Temple, the same as the seasonal sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: A day was chosen for a visit to the Grand Ancestral Temple, following the seasonal sacrifice ceremony.

sentences.zh: 明日，百官公服稱賀，賜宴謹身殿。

translations.literal: On the following day, the hundred officials in formal dress offered congratulations; a banquet was granted at the Hall of Self-Cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: The next day officials in formal dress offered congratulations, and a banquet was granted at the Hall of Self-Cultivation.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三年正月，帝擇日長髮，命禮部具儀。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Wanli, the emperor chose a day to let his hair grow long and ordered the Ministry of Rites to prepare the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Wanli the emperor chose an auspicious day to let his hair grow long and ordered the Ministry of Rites to prepare the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 大學士張居正等言：「禮重冠婚，皇上前在東宮已行冠禮，三加稱尊，執爵而酳。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Zhang Juzheng and others said: "The rites value capping and marriage; His Majesty previously in the Eastern Palace already performed the capping rite, with three investitures conferring honor, holding the goblet for palate-cleansing.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Zhang Juzheng and others said: "The rites attach great weight to capping and marriage. His Majesty, while still in the Eastern Palace, has already undergone the capping ceremony with three investitures conferring titles of honor and the goblet for palate-cleansing.

sentences.zh: 巨禮既成，可略其細。

translations.literal: The great rite being already complete, minor details may be omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Since the great ceremony is already complete, the minor details may be omitted.

sentences.zh: 不必命部臣擬議。

translations.literal: There is no need to order ministry officials to draft proposals.
translations.idiomatic: There is no need to order ministry officials to draft proposals.

sentences.zh: 第先期至奉先殿、弘孝殿、神霄殿以長髮告。

translations.literal: Only beforehand go to the Hall of Veneration of Ancestors, the Hall of Grand Filiality, and the Hall of Divine Azure to announce letting the hair grow long.
translations.idiomatic: It is enough to go beforehand to the Hall of Veneration of Ancestors, the Hall of Grand Filiality, and the Hall of Divine Azure to announce that the hair is being let grow long.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，詣兩宮皇太后，行五拜三叩頭禮，隨御乾清宮受賀。

translations.literal: When the rite was finished, go to both palaces of the Empress Dowager and perform the five-bow and three-kowtow rite, then attend the Palace of Heavenly Purity to receive congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When that ceremony is finished, he should go to both palaces of the Empress Dowager and perform five bows and three kowtows, then proceed to the Palace of Heavenly Purity to receive congratulations.

sentences.zh: 」帝是之，遂著爲令。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved this and established it as a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved this and established it as a regulation.

sentences.zh: 皇太子皇子冠禮

translations.literal: Crowning rites for the crown prince and imperial sons
translations.idiomatic: Crowning the Crown Prince and Imperial Sons

sentences.zh: 《禮》曰：「冠於阼，以著代也。

translations.literal: The Rites says: "Capping at the eastern steps is to show succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites says: "Capping at the eastern steps marks the transfer of succession.

sentences.zh: 醮於客位，三加彌尊，加有成也。

translations.literal: Libation at the guest position; three investitures increasingly honored; each investiture signifies completion.
translations.idiomatic: The libation at the guest position and three investitures, each more honored than the last, show that each stage brings the rite toward completion.

sentences.zh: 已冠而字之，成人之道也。

translations.literal: After capping, bestow a courtesy name—this is the way of adulthood.
translations.idiomatic: After capping one bestows a courtesy name—this is the way of adulthood.

sentences.zh: 」「雖天子之元子，猶士也。

translations.literal: " "Even the eldest son of the Son of Heaven is still like a common gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: "Even the eldest son of the Son of Heaven is still treated like a common gentleman."

sentences.zh: 」其禮歷代用之。

translations.literal: " This rite was used through successive dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: This rite was used through successive dynasties.

sentences.zh: 明皇太子加元服，參用周文王、成王冠禮之年，近則十二，遠則十五。

translations.literal: For the Ming crown prince's capping investiture, reference was made to the ages at which King Wen and King Cheng of Zhou underwent the capping rite: as early as twelve, as late as fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: For the Ming crown prince's coming-of-age ceremony, the ages at which King Wen and King Cheng of Zhou underwent the capping rite were taken as reference: as early as twelve and as late as fifteen.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十四年，穆宗在東宮，方十歲，欲行冠禮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Jiajing, Muzong was in the Eastern Palace, just ten years old, and wished to perform the capping rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Jiajing, Muzong was in the Eastern Palace at just ten years of age and wished to undergo the capping ceremony.

sentences.zh: 大學士嚴嵩、尚書費寀初皆難之，後遂阿旨以爲可行，而請稍簡煩儀，止取成禮。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Yan Song and Minister Fei Cai at first all found it difficult, but later agreed to the imperial wish and deemed it feasible, requesting that the cumbersome ceremony be slightly simplified and only the completed rite be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Yan Song and Minister Fei Cai initially opposed the idea, but later acceded to the imperial wish and deemed it feasible, requesting that the cumbersome ceremony be simplified and only the essential rite retained.

sentences.zh: 帝以冠當具禮，至二十八年始行之。

translations.literal: The emperor held that capping should have the full ceremony; only in the twenty-eighth year was it performed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that the capping should be performed with the full ceremony, and it was not carried out until the twenty-eighth year.

sentences.zh: 其儀洪武元年定。

translations.literal: Its regulations were fixed in the first year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: The regulations were established in the first year of Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 前期，太史監卜日，工部置袞冕諸服，翰林院撰祝文。

translations.literal: Beforehand, the Directorate of Astronomy divined the day; the Ministry of Works prepared sacrificial robes and various garments; the Hanlin Academy drafted the prayer text.
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand the Directorate of Astronomy divined the auspicious day, the Ministry of Works prepared the sacrificial robes and other garments, and the Hanlin Academy drafted the prayer text.

sentences.zh: 中書省承制。

translations.literal: The Secretariat received the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat received the imperial command.

sentences.zh: 命某官爲賓，某官贊。

translations.literal: Such-and-such official was appointed guest; such-and-such official was appointed announcer.
translations.idiomatic: Such-and-such official was appointed guest, and such-and-such official announcer.

sentences.zh: 既卜日，遣官告天地宗廟。

translations.literal: Once the day was divined, officials were dispatched to announce to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Once the day was chosen, officials were dispatched to announce the event to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 前一日，陳御座香案於奉天殿，設皇太子次於殿東房，賓贊次於午門外。

translations.literal: The day before, the imperial throne and incense table were set out in the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the crown prince's waiting place was set in the hall's eastern side room; the guest and announcer waited outside the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the ceremony, the imperial throne and incense table were set out in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, the crown prince's waiting place in the hall's eastern side room, and the guest and announcer waited outside the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 質明，執事官設罍洗於東階，設皇太子冠席於殿上東南，西向，設醴席於西階上，南向，張帷幄於東序內，設褥席於帷中，又張帷於序外。

translations.literal: At dawn, officiating officials set the ablution vessel at the eastern steps, the crown prince's capping mat southeast on the hall facing west, the ritual wine mat on the western steps facing south; canopies were spread within the eastern wing with a mat inside, and another canopy was spread outside the wing.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn officiating officials set the ablution vessel at the eastern steps, the crown prince's capping mat in the hall's southeast facing west, and the ritual wine mat on the western steps facing south; canopies were spread in the eastern wing with a mat inside, and another canopy outside the wing.

sentences.zh: 御用監陳服於帷內東，領北上，袞服九章、遠遊冠、絳紗袍、折上巾、緇纚犀簪在服南，櫛又在南。

translations.literal: The Imperial Workshop displayed garments east inside the canopy with the collar facing north: sacrificial robes with nine emblems, the Far-Traveling Coronet, crimson gauze robe, folded-up cap, black cap strings, and rhinoceros hairpin south of the robes, with the comb further south.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Workshop laid out the garments on the east side inside the canopy, collars facing north: sacrificial robes with nine emblems, the Far-Traveling Coronet, crimson gauze robe, folded-up cap, black cap strings, and rhinoceros hairpin south of the robes, with the comb further south.

sentences.zh: 司尊實醴於側尊，加勺冪，設於醴席之南。

translations.literal: The director of vessels filled the side urn with ritual wine, added ladle and cover, and set it south of the ritual wine mat.
translations.idiomatic: The director of vessels filled the side urn with ritual wine, added the ladle and cover, and placed it south of the ritual wine mat.

sentences.zh: 設坫於尊東，置二爵。

translations.literal: A spirit stand was set east of the urn, and two goblets were placed on it.
translations.idiomatic: A spirit stand was placed east of the urn with two goblets upon it.

sentences.zh: 進饌者實饌，設於尊北。

translations.literal: The food presenter filled the food offering and set it north of the urn.
translations.idiomatic: The food presenter filled the food offering and placed it north of the urn.

sentences.zh: 諸執事者各立其所。

translations.literal: All functionaries stood at their respective positions.
translations.idiomatic: All functionaries took up their respective positions.

sentences.zh: 鼓三嚴，文武官入。

translations.literal: The drum sounded three rounds of vigil; civil and military officials entered.
translations.idiomatic: After the triple drum signal marking the third watch of vigil, civil and military officials entered.

sentences.zh: 皇帝服通天冠、絳紗袍，升座如常儀。

translations.literal: The emperor wore the Heaven-Penetrating Coronet and crimson gauze robe and ascended the throne as in the usual rite.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore the Heaven-Penetrating Coronet and crimson gauze robe and ascended the throne according to the usual ceremony.

sentences.zh: 賓贊就位，樂作。

translations.literal: The guest and announcer took their positions; music began.
translations.idiomatic: The guest and announcer took their positions as music began.

sentences.zh: 四拜興，樂止。

translations.literal: Four prostrations and rising; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: They performed four prostrations and rose; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 侍儀司跪承制，降至東階，詣賓前，稱有敕。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Ceremonial Attendants knelt to receive the edict, descended to the eastern steps, went before the guest, and announced that there was an imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Ceremonial Attendants knelt to receive the imperial command, descended to the eastern steps, went before the guest, and announced that an edict was forthcoming.

sentences.zh: 賓贊及在位官皆跪。

translations.literal: The guest, announcer, and officials in attendance all knelt.
translations.idiomatic: The guest, announcer, and officials in attendance all knelt.

sentences.zh: 宣制曰：「皇太子冠，命卿等行禮。

translations.literal: The edict was proclaimed, saying: "The crown prince is to be capped; you are commanded to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was proclaimed: "The crown prince is to be capped; you are commanded to perform the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 」皆俯伏，興，四拜。

translations.literal: " All bowed low, rose, and performed four prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: All bowed low, rose, and performed four prostrations.

sentences.zh: 文武侍從班俱就殿內位，賓贊執事官詣東階下位。

translations.literal: The civil and military attendant ranks all took positions inside the hall; the guest, announcer, and functionaries went to positions below the eastern steps.
translations.idiomatic: The civil and military attendant ranks all took their places inside the hall, while the guest, announcer, and functionaries went to positions below the eastern steps.

sentences.zh: 東宮官及太常博士詣殿前東房，導皇太子入就冠席，二內侍夾侍，東宮官後從，樂作。

translations.literal: Eastern Palace officials and the Grand Master of Sacrifices went to the eastern side room before the hall, guided the crown prince in to the capping mat; two inner attendants attended on either side, Eastern Palace officials following behind; music began.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Palace officials and the Grand Master of Sacrifices went to the hall's eastern side room and guided the crown prince to the capping mat; two inner attendants flanked him with Eastern Palace officials following behind as music began.

sentences.zh: 即席西南向，樂止。

translations.literal: He took his seat facing southwest; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He took his seat facing southwest, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 賓贊以次詣罍洗，樂作。

translations.literal: The guest and announcer in order went to the ablution vessel; music began.
translations.idiomatic: The guest and announcer proceeded in turn to the ablution vessel as music began.

sentences.zh: 搢笏，盥帨，出笏，樂止。

translations.literal: They inserted their tablets, washed and dried their hands, and removed their tablets; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: They inserted their tablets, washed and dried their hands, removed their tablets, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 升自西階，執事者奉折上巾進，賓降一等受之。

translations.literal: They ascended by the western steps; a functionary presented the folded-up cap; the guest descended one step rank to receive it.
translations.idiomatic: They ascended the western steps; a functionary presented the folded-up cap, and the guest descended one step to receive it.

sentences.zh: 右執項，左執前，進太子席前，北面祝畢，跪冠，樂作。

translations.literal: Right hand holding the back, left hand holding the front, he advanced before the crown prince's mat; facing north, when the prayer was finished he knelt to crown him; music began.
translations.idiomatic: Holding the back with his right hand and the front with his left, he advanced before the crown prince's mat; facing north, he finished the prayer, knelt, and placed the cap as music began.

sentences.zh: 賓興，席南北面立。

translations.literal: The guest rose and stood north of the mat facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The guest rose and stood north of the mat, facing south.

sentences.zh: 贊冠者進席前，北面跪，正冠，興，立於賓後。

translations.literal: The crown assistant advanced before the mat, knelt facing north, straightened the coronet, rose, and stood behind the guest.
translations.idiomatic: The crown assistant advanced before the mat, knelt facing north, straightened the coronet, rose, and stood behind the guest.

sentences.zh: 內侍跪進服，皇太子興，服訖，樂止。

translations.literal: An inner attendant knelt and presented the robe; the crown prince rose; when robed, music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: An inner attendant knelt and presented the robe; the crown prince rose, and when he had finished dressing, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 賓揖皇太子復坐。

translations.literal: The guest bowed to the crown prince, who resumed his seat.
translations.idiomatic: The guest bowed to the crown prince, who resumed his seat.

sentences.zh: 賓贊降，詣罍洗訖，贊進前跪，脫折上巾，置於箱，興，以授內侍。

translations.literal: The guest and announcer descended, went to the ablution vessel; when finished, the announcer advanced, knelt, removed the folded-up cap, placed it in a box, rose, and handed it to an inner attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The guest and announcer descended and went to the ablution vessel; when finished, the announcer advanced, knelt, removed the folded-up cap, placed it in a box, rose, and handed it to an inner attendant.

sentences.zh: 執事者奉遠遊冠進，賓降二等受之，樂作，進冠如前儀。

translations.literal: A functionary presented the Far-Traveling Coronet; the guest descended two step ranks to receive it; music began; he advanced to crown him as in the previous rite.
translations.idiomatic: A functionary presented the Far-Traveling Coronet; the guest descended two steps to receive it; music began, and he advanced to crown the prince as in the previous stage.

sentences.zh: 贊進前，北面跪，簪結紘，內侍跪進服，樂止。

translations.literal: The announcer advanced, knelt facing north, pinned and tied the cap strings; an inner attendant knelt and presented the robe; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer advanced, knelt facing north, pinned and tied the cap strings; an inner attendant knelt and presented the robe, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 賓揖皇太子復坐。

translations.literal: The guest bowed to the crown prince, who resumed his seat.
translations.idiomatic: The guest bowed to the crown prince, who resumed his seat.

sentences.zh: 又詣罍洗，贊脫冠，執事者奉袞冕進，賓降三等受之，樂作。

translations.literal: Again they went to the ablution vessel; the announcer removed the coronet; a functionary presented the sacrificial coronet and robes; the guest descended three step ranks to receive them; music began.
translations.idiomatic: They again went to the ablution vessel; the announcer removed the coronet; a functionary presented the sacrificial coronet and robes; the guest descended three steps to receive them as music began.

sentences.zh: 進冠結紘，內侍跪進服，如前儀，樂止。

translations.literal: He advanced to crown him and tie the cap strings; an inner attendant knelt and presented the robe, as in the previous rite; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to crown him and tie the cap strings; an inner attendant knelt and presented the robe as in the previous stage, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 太常博士導皇太子降自東階，樂作。

translations.literal: The Grand Master of Sacrifices guided the crown prince down by the eastern steps; music began.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Master of Sacrifices guided the crown prince down the eastern steps as music began.

sentences.zh: 由西階升，即醴席，南向坐，樂止。

translations.literal: He ascended by the western steps, took the ritual wine mat, and sat facing south; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He ascended the western steps, took his place at the ritual wine mat facing south, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 賓詣罍洗盥帨訖，贊冠者取爵、盥爵、帨爵，詣司尊所酌醴，授賓。

translations.literal: The guest went to the ablution vessel and finished washing and drying; the crown assistant took the goblet, washed the goblet, dried the goblet, went to the director of vessels to pour ritual wine, and handed it to the guest.
translations.idiomatic: The guest went to the ablution vessel and finished washing and drying his hands; the crown assistant took the goblet, washed and dried it, went to the director of vessels to pour ritual wine, and handed it to the guest.

sentences.zh: 賓受爵，跪進於皇太子。

translations.literal: The guest received the goblet and knelt to present it to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The guest received the goblet and knelt to present it to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 祝畢，皇太子搢圭，跪受爵，樂作。

translations.literal: When the prayer was finished, the crown prince inserted his scepter, knelt to receive the goblet; music began.
translations.idiomatic: When the prayer was finished, the crown prince inserted his scepter, knelt to receive the goblet, and music began.

sentences.zh: 飲訖，奠爵，執圭。

translations.literal: When drinking was finished, he set down the goblet and held the scepter.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished drinking, he set down the goblet and held the scepter.

sentences.zh: 進饌者奉饌於前，皇太子搢圭，食訖，執圭，興，樂止。

translations.literal: The food presenter presented food before him; the crown prince inserted his scepter; when eating was finished, he held the scepter and rose; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The food presenter presented food before him; the crown prince inserted his scepter; when he had finished eating, he held the scepter and rose, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 徹爵與饌。

translations.literal: The goblet and food were removed.
translations.idiomatic: The goblet and food were removed.

sentences.zh: 博士導皇太子降自西階，至殿東房，易朝服，詣丹墀拜位，北向。

translations.literal: The master guided the crown prince down by the western steps to the hall's eastern side room, changed into court dress, and went to the prostration position on the red courtyard facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The master guided the crown prince down the western steps to the hall's eastern side room, where he changed into court dress, then went to the obeisance position on the red courtyard facing north.

sentences.zh: 東宮官屬各復拜位。

translations.literal: Eastern Palace staff each returned to their prostration positions.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Palace staff each returned to their obeisance positions.

sentences.zh: 賓贊詣皇太子位稍東，西向。

translations.literal: The guest and announcer went slightly east of the crown prince's position, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The guest and announcer went to a position slightly east of the crown prince, facing west.

sentences.zh: 賓少進字之辭曰：「奉敕字某。

translations.literal: The guest slightly advanced and spoke the words for bestowing the courtesy name: "By imperial command, the courtesy name So-and-so.
translations.idiomatic: The guest slightly advanced and spoke the words for bestowing the courtesy name: "By imperial command, the courtesy name is So-and-so.

sentences.zh: 」皇太子再拜，跪聽宣敕。

translations.literal: " The crown prince performed two prostrations, knelt, and listened to the imperial command proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince performed two prostrations, knelt, and listened to the imperial command.

sentences.zh: 復再拜，興。

translations.literal: Again two prostrations; he rose.
translations.idiomatic: He performed two more prostrations and rose.

sentences.zh: 進御前跪奏曰：「臣不敏，敢不祗承。

translations.literal: He advanced before the throne, knelt, and reported: "Your subject is unworthy; how dare I not respectfully accept.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced before the throne, knelt, and reported: "Your subject is unworthy; how dare I not respectfully accept.

sentences.zh: 」奏畢，復位。

translations.literal: " When the report was finished, he returned to his position.
translations.idiomatic: When the report was finished, he returned to his place.

sentences.zh: 侍立官並降殿復位，四拜禮畢，皇帝興。

translations.literal: Attendant officials all descended from the hall and returned to their positions; four prostrations—the rite was complete; the emperor rose.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant officials all descended from the hall and returned to their places; after four prostrations the ceremony was complete, and the emperor rose.

sentences.zh: 內給事導皇太子入內殿，見皇后，如正旦儀。

translations.literal: An inner chamberlain guided the crown prince into the inner hall to see the empress, as in the New Year's Day rite.
translations.idiomatic: An inner chamberlain guided the crown prince into the inner hall to see the empress according to the New Year's Day ceremony.

sentences.zh: 明日謁廟，如時享禮。

translations.literal: The next day he visited the temple, as in the seasonal offering rite.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he visited the ancestral temple according to the seasonal offering ceremony.

sentences.zh: 又明日，百官朝服詣奉天殿稱賀，退易公服，詣東宮稱賀，錫宴。

translations.literal: On the day after that, the hundred officials in court dress went to the Hall of Supreme Harmony to offer congratulations; they withdrew, changed into formal dress, went to the Eastern Palace to offer congratulations, and a banquet was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On the following day officials in court dress went to the Hall of Supreme Harmony to offer congratulations; they then withdrew, changed into formal dress, went to the Eastern Palace to offer congratulations, and a banquet was granted.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年，續定皇太子冠禮。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chenghua, the crown prince capping rite was revised.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Chenghua the crown prince capping ceremony was revised.

sentences.zh: 先日，設幕次於文華殿東序，設節案、香案、冠席、醴席、盥洗、司尊所等，具如儀。

translations.literal: On the previous day, a tent was set in the eastern wing of the Hall of Literary Glory; tally table, incense table, capping mat, ritual wine mat, ablution place, director of vessels station, and the like were all prepared as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: On the previous day a tent was set up in the eastern wing of the Hall of Literary Glory, with the tally table, incense table, capping mat, ritual wine mat, ablution place, director of vessels station, and the like all prepared according to the prescribed rite.

sentences.zh: 內侍張帷幄，陳袍服、皮弁服、袞服、圭帶、舄、翼善冠、皮弁、九旒冕。

translations.literal: Inner attendants spread canopies and displayed robe garments, leather-cap attire, sacrificial robes, scepter and belt, shoes, Good-Wing Coronet, leather cap, and nine-tassel coronet.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants spread canopies and laid out robe garments, leather-cap attire, sacrificial robes, scepter and belt, shoes, the Good-Wing Coronet, leather cap, and nine-tassel coronet.

sentences.zh: 質明，皇帝御奉天殿傳制，遣官持節。

translations.literal: At dawn, the emperor attended the Hall of Supreme Harmony to transmit the edict and dispatched an official bearing the tally.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the emperor took his place in the Hall of Supreme Harmony to transmit the edict and dispatched an official bearing the tally.

sentences.zh: 皇太子迎於文華殿門外，捧入，置於案，退。

translations.literal: The crown prince received it outside the gate of the Hall of Literary Glory, bore it in, placed it on the table, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince received the tally outside the gate of the Hall of Literary Glory, bore it in, placed it on the table, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 禮部官導皇太子詣香案前，樂作。

translations.literal: A Ministry of Rites official guided the crown prince before the incense table; music began.
translations.idiomatic: A Ministry of Rites official guided the crown prince before the incense table as music began.

sentences.zh: 四拜，樂止。

translations.literal: Four prostrations; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He performed four prostrations, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 行初加冠禮。

translations.literal: The first capping investiture rite was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The first capping investiture was performed.

sentences.zh: 內侍奉翼善冠，賓祝曰：「吉月令辰，乃加元服。

translations.literal: Inner attendants presented the Good-Wing Coronet; the guest intoned the prayer: "On this auspicious day at the auspicious hour, the capping investiture is bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants presented the Good-Wing Coronet, and the guest intoned the prayer: "On this auspicious day and hour, the capping investiture begins.

sentences.zh: 懋敬是承，永介景福。

translations.literal: May you earnestly accept reverence, and ever receive great blessing.
translations.idiomatic: May you bear reverence upon you and ever receive Heaven's abundant blessing.

sentences.zh: 」樂作。

translations.literal: " Music began.
translations.idiomatic: Music began.

sentences.zh: 賓跪進冠，興，樂止。

translations.literal: The guest knelt and presented the coronet; rose; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The guest knelt and presented the coronet, then rose as the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 禮部官啓易服，皇太子入幄，易袍服出，啓復坐。

translations.literal: A Ministry of Rites official reported a request to change garments; the crown prince entered the canopy, changed into robe garments and came out, reported, and resumed his seat.
translations.idiomatic: A Ministry of Rites official reported a request for a change of garments; the crown prince entered the canopy, changed into robe garments, came out, reported back, and resumed his seat.

sentences.zh: 行再加冠禮。

translations.literal: The second capping investiture rite was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The second capping investiture was performed.

sentences.zh: 內侍奉皮弁，賓祝曰：「冠禮申舉，以成令德。

translations.literal: Inner attendants presented the leather cap; the guest intoned the prayer: "The capping rite is solemnly raised, to complete excellent virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants presented the leather cap, and the guest intoned the prayer: "The capping rite is now solemnly performed, to complete your excellent virtue.

sentences.zh: 敬慎威儀，惟民之式。

translations.literal: Reverent and cautious in dignity and bearing, a model for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Be reverent and cautious in dignity and bearing, a model for the people.

sentences.zh: 」冠畢，入幄，易皮弁服舄出，啓復坐。

translations.literal: " When the crowning was finished, he entered the canopy, changed into leather-cap attire and shoes and came out, reported, and resumed his seat.
translations.idiomatic: When the crowning was finished, he entered the canopy, changed into leather-cap attire and shoes, came out, reported back, and resumed his seat.

sentences.zh: 行三加冠禮。

translations.literal: The third capping investiture rite was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The third capping investiture was performed.

sentences.zh: 內侍奉冕旒，賓祝曰：「章服鹹加，飭敬有虔。

translations.literal: Inner attendants presented the coronet with tassels; the guest intoned the prayer: "Regalia and robes all added, adorned with reverent devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants presented the coronet with tassels, and the guest intoned the prayer: "Regalia and robes are all now bestowed; perform the rite with adorned reverence and devotion.

sentences.zh: 永固皇圖，於千萬年。

translations.literal: May the royal design endure for ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: May the royal design endure for ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 」冠畢，入幄，易袞服出，啓復坐。

translations.literal: " When the crowning was finished, he entered the canopy, changed into sacrificial robes and came out, reported, and resumed his seat.
translations.idiomatic: When the crowning was finished, he entered the canopy, changed into sacrificial robes, came out, reported back, and resumed his seat.

sentences.zh: 行醮禮，皇太子詣醴席，樂作。

translations.literal: The libation rite was performed; the crown prince went to the ritual wine mat; music began.
translations.idiomatic: The libation rite was performed; the crown prince proceeded to the ritual wine mat as music began.

sentences.zh: 即坐，樂止。

translations.literal: He immediately sat; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He took his seat, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 光祿寺官舉醴案，樂作。

translations.literal: An official of the Directorate of Imperial Banquets raised the ritual wine table; music began.
translations.idiomatic: An official of the Directorate of Imperial Banquets presented the ritual wine table as music began.

sentences.zh: 贊酌醴授賓，賓執爵詣席前，樂止。

translations.literal: The announcer called to pour the ritual wine and hand it to the guest; the guest took the goblet and went before the mat; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer called for the ritual wine to be poured and handed to the guest; the guest took the goblet and went before the mat as the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 賓祝曰：「旨酒孔馨，加薦再芳。

translations.literal: The guest intoned the prayer: "The fine wine is very fragrant; offered again with doubled fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: The guest intoned the prayer: "The fine wine is richly fragrant; offered again with redoubled fragrance.

sentences.zh: 受天之福，萬世其昌。

translations.literal: Receive Heaven's blessing; may you flourish for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Receive Heaven's blessing; may your line flourish for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 」賓跪進爵，皇太子搢圭，受爵，置於案。

translations.literal: " The guest knelt and presented the goblet; the crown prince inserted his scepter, received the goblet, and placed it on the table.
translations.idiomatic: The guest knelt and presented the goblet; the crown prince inserted his scepter, received the goblet, and set it on the table.

sentences.zh: 教坊司作樂，奏《喜千春之曲》。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Music performed music, playing "The Melody of Joyful Thousand Springs."
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Music performed, playing "The Melody of Joyful Thousand Springs."

sentences.zh: 次啓進酒，皇太子舉爵飲訖，奠爵於案，樂止。

translations.literal: Next a report was made to present wine; the crown prince raised the goblet, drank to completion, set the goblet on the table; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Next a report was made to present wine; the crown prince raised the goblet, drank it dry, placed the goblet on the table, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 光祿寺官進饌，樂作。

translations.literal: An official of the Directorate of Imperial Banquets presented food; music began.
translations.idiomatic: An official of the Directorate of Imperial Banquets presented the food as music began.

sentences.zh: 至案，樂止。

translations.literal: When he reached the table, music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the table, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 饌訖，出圭，徹案，賓贊復位。

translations.literal: When the food was finished, he removed his scepter; the table was cleared; the guest and announcer returned to their positions.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished the food, he removed his scepter; the table was cleared; and the guest and announcer returned to their positions.

sentences.zh: 鳴贊贊受敕戒。

translations.literal: The chief announcer called for receiving the admonitory command.
translations.idiomatic: The chief announcer called for the admonitory command to be received.

sentences.zh: 皇太子降階，樂作。

translations.literal: The crown prince descended the steps; music began.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince descended the steps as music began.

sentences.zh: 至拜位，樂止。

translations.literal: When he reached the prostration position, music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the obeisance position, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 宣敕戒官詣皇太子前稍東，西向立，曰：「有制」。

translations.literal: The official proclaiming the admonitory command went slightly east before the crown prince, stood facing west, and said: "There is an imperial command."
translations.idiomatic: The official charged with proclaiming the admonitory command went to a position slightly east of the crown prince, stood facing west, and said: "There is an imperial command."

sentences.zh: 皇太子跪，宣敕戒曰：「孝事君親，友于兄弟。

translations.literal: The crown prince knelt; the admonitory command was proclaimed: "Serve your sovereign and parents with filial piety; be friendly to your brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince knelt as the admonitory command was proclaimed: "Serve your sovereign and parents with filial piety; be friendly to your brothers.

sentences.zh: 親賢愛民，居由仁義。

translations.literal: Draw near to the worthy and love the people; conduct yourself through benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Cherish the worthy and love the people; let your conduct be governed by benevolence and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 毋怠毋驕，茂隆萬世。

translations.literal: Do not slacken, do not be arrogant; may your flourishing endure for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Be neither slack nor arrogant; may your flourishing endure for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 」樂作。

translations.literal: " Music began.
translations.idiomatic: Music began.

sentences.zh: 四拜興，樂止。

translations.literal: Four prostrations and rise; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He performed four prostrations and rose as the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 持節官捧節出，樂作。

translations.literal: The official bearing the tally held the tally and went out; music began.
translations.idiomatic: The official bearing the tally carried the tally out as music began.

sentences.zh: 皇太子送節至殿門外，還東序。

translations.literal: The crown prince escorted the tally to outside the hall gate and returned to the eastern wing.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince escorted the tally to outside the hall gate and returned to the eastern wing.

sentences.zh: 內侍導還宮，樂止。

translations.literal: Inner attendants guided him back to the palace; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants guided him back to the palace, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 賓贊等官持節覆命，餘如舊儀。

translations.literal: The guest, announcer, and other officials bore the tally to report completion; the rest followed the old rite.
translations.idiomatic: The guest, announcer, and other officials bore the tally back to report completion; the remainder followed the established rite.

sentences.zh: 是日，皇太子詣皇太后、皇帝、皇后前謝，俱行五拜三叩頭禮，用樂。

translations.literal: That day, the crown prince went before the empress dowager, emperor, and empress to offer thanks; all performed the rite of five bows and three kowtows, with music.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the crown prince went before the empress dowager, emperor, and empress to offer thanks; before each he performed five bows and three kowtows, with music.

sentences.zh: 明日，皇帝及皇太子受羣臣賀，如儀。

translations.literal: The next day, the emperor and crown prince received congratulations from the assembled officials, as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor and crown prince received congratulations from the assembled officials according to the prescribed ceremony.

sentences.zh: 皇子冠禮。

translations.literal: The capping rite of imperial sons.
translations.idiomatic: The Capping Rite of Imperial Sons.

sentences.zh: 初加，進網巾，祝詞曰：「茲惟吉日，冠以成人。

translations.literal: At the first investiture, the net cap was presented; the prayer text read: "On this auspicious day, the crown marks one come of age.
translations.idiomatic: At the first investiture the net cap was presented; the prayer read: "On this auspicious day the crown marks your passage into manhood.

sentences.zh: 克敦孝友，福祿來駢。

translations.literal: Be able to practice filial piety and brotherly affection; may blessings and emoluments come paired.
translations.idiomatic: May you be steadfast in filial piety and brotherly affection; may blessings and emolument come in abundance.

sentences.zh: 」再加，進翼善冠，祝詞曰：「冠禮斯舉，賓由成德。

translations.literal: " At the second investiture, the Good-Wing Coronet was presented; the prayer text read: "The capping rite is now performed; through the guest complete your virtue.
translations.idiomatic: At the second investiture the Good-Wing Coronet was presented; the prayer read: "The capping rite is now performed; through this ritual complete your virtue.

sentences.zh: 敬慎威儀，維民之則。

translations.literal: Reverent and cautious in dignity and bearing, a rule for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Be reverent and cautious in dignity and bearing, a standard for the people.

sentences.zh: 」三加，進袞冕，祝詞曰：「冠至三加，命服用章。

translations.literal: " At the third investiture, sacrificial coronet and robes were presented; the prayer text read: "The crown reaches the third investiture; orders and garments assume their emblems.
translations.idiomatic: At the third investiture the sacrificial coronet and robes were presented; the prayer read: "With the crown at the third investiture, rank and regalia take their proper emblems.

sentences.zh: 敬神事上，永固籓邦。

translations.literal: Reverence the spirits and serve your superiors; may your fiefdom be forever secure.
translations.idiomatic: Revere the spirits and serve your sovereign; may your princely domain endure forever.

sentences.zh: 」酌醴祝曰：「旨酒嘉薦，載芬載芳。

translations.literal: " When pouring the ritual wine the prayer read: "Fine wine offered in excellent sacrifice, laden with fragrance upon fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: When pouring the ritual wine the prayer read: "Fine wine offered in excellent sacrifice, redolent with fragrance.

sentences.zh: 受茲景福，百世其昌。

translations.literal: Receive this great blessing; may you flourish for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Receive this great blessing; may your line flourish for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 」敕戒詞曰：「孝於君親，友于兄弟。

translations.literal: " The admonitory command read: "Be filial toward sovereign and parents; be friendly to brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The admonitory command read: "Be filial toward your sovereign and parents; be friendly to your brothers.

sentences.zh: 親賢愛民，率由禮義。

translations.literal: Draw near to the worthy and love the people; follow the path of ritual and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Cherish the worthy and love the people; let your conduct be guided by ritual and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 毋溢毋驕，永保富貴。

translations.literal: Do not overstep, do not be arrogant; may you forever preserve wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Do not overstep your bounds or grow arrogant; may you forever preserve wealth and honor.

sentences.zh: 」其陳設執事及傳制謁謝，並如皇太子儀。

translations.literal: " The arrangements, functionaries, transmission of edicts, and presentation of thanks all followed the crown prince rite.
translations.idiomatic: The arrangements, functionaries, transmission of edicts, and presentation of thanks all followed the crown prince ceremony.

sentences.zh: 初，皇子冠之明日，百官稱賀畢，詣王府行禮。

translations.literal: Originally, on the day after an imperial son's capping, after the hundred officials had offered congratulations, they went to the princely residence to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Originally, on the day following an imperial son's capping, after officials had offered their congratulations they went to the princely residence to perform the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 成化二十三年，皇子冠之次日，各詣奉天門東廡序坐，百官常服四拜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Chenghua, on the day after an imperial son's capping, each went to the eastern corridor of the Gate of Receiving Heaven and took seats in order; the hundred officials in ordinary dress performed four prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Chenghua, on the day following an imperial son's capping, each went to the eastern corridor of the Gate of Receiving Heaven and took seats in order; officials in ordinary dress performed four prostrations.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十九年，禮部尚書馮琦言：「舊制皇太子冠，設冠席、醴席於文華殿內。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Wanli, Minister of Rites Feng Qi said: "Under the old system, for the crown prince's capping, capping and ritual wine mats were set inside the Hall of Literary Glory.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of Wanli, Minister of Rites Feng Qi stated: "Under the old regulations, at the crown prince's capping the capping mat and ritual wine mat were set inside the Hall of Literary Glory.

sentences.zh: 今文華殿爲皇上臨御遣官之地，則皇太子冠醴席，應移於殿之東序。

translations.literal: Now the Hall of Literary Glory is where His Majesty attends to dispatch officials; therefore the crown prince's capping and ritual wine mats should be moved to the hall's eastern wing.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Hall of Literary Glory is where His Majesty takes his seat to dispatch officials, the crown prince's capping and ritual wine mats should be moved to the hall's eastern wing.

sentences.zh: 又親王冠，舊設席於皇極門之東廡。

translations.literal: Also, for capping of princes of the blood, mats were formerly set in the eastern corridor of the Gate of Imperial Supremacy.
translations.idiomatic: For the capping of princes of the blood, mats were formerly set in the eastern corridor of the Gate of Imperial Supremacy.

sentences.zh: 今皇太子移席於殿東序，則親王應移席於殿西序。

translations.literal: Now that the crown prince's mats are moved to the hall's eastern wing, princes of the blood should move their mats to the hall's western wing.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the crown prince's mats are moved to the hall's eastern wing, princes of the blood should move their mats to the hall's western wing.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 永樂九年十一月，命皇太子嫡長子爲皇太孫，冠於華蓋殿，其儀與皇太子同。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the ninth year of Yongle, the crown prince's eldest legitimate son was appointed imperial grand heir; he was capped in the Hall of Flowering Canopy; the rite was the same as for the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the ninth year of Yongle, the crown prince's eldest legitimate son was appointed imperial grand heir and capped in the Hall of Flowering Canopy; the ceremony was the same as for the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 品官冠禮

translations.literal: Capping Rite of Ranked Officials
translations.idiomatic: The Capping Rite of Ranked Officials

sentences.zh: 古者男子二十而冠，大夫五十而後爵，故無大夫冠禮。

translations.literal: In antiquity a man capped at twenty; a grand officer received ennoblement only after fifty; therefore there was no capping rite for grand officers.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity men underwent the capping ceremony at twenty, and grand officers received nobility only after fifty; accordingly there was no capping rite for grand officers.

sentences.zh: 唐制，三加，一品之子以袞冕，逮九品之子以爵弁，皆仿士禮而增益之。

translations.literal: Under Tang regulations, three investitures: sons of first rank wore sacrificial coronet and robes; down to sons of ninth rank wore noble cap; all followed the scholar's rite with additions.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang regulations there were three investitures: sons of first-rank officials wore sacrificial coronet and robes, while those of ninth rank and above wore the noble cap; all followed the scholar's rite with additions.

sentences.zh: 明洪武元年定制，始加緇布冠，再加進賢冠，三加爵弁。

translations.literal: Regulations established in the first year of Hongwu of Ming: first investiture, black cloth cap; second investiture, Scholar-Aspiring Coronet; third investiture, noble cap.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations established in the first year of Hongwu specified: first investiture with the black cloth cap, second with the Scholar-Aspiring Coronet, and third with the noble cap.

sentences.zh: 其儀，前期擇日，主者告於家廟，乃筮賓。

translations.literal: As for the rite, beforehand a day was chosen; the host reported to the family temple, then divined for a guest.
translations.idiomatic: As for the ceremony, beforehand an auspicious day was chosen; the host reported to the family temple, then divined for a guest.

sentences.zh: 前二日，戒賓及贊冠者。

translations.literal: Two days before, the guest and crown announcer were given notice.
translations.idiomatic: Two days before, the guest and crown announcer were notified.

sentences.zh: 明日，設次於大門外之右，南向。

translations.literal: The next day, a tent was set outside the great gate to the right, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The next day a tent was set up to the right outside the main gate, facing south.

sentences.zh: 至日，夙興，設洗於阼階東南，東西當東霤，六品以下當東榮，南北以堂深。

translations.literal: On the day itself, rising early, ablution was set southeast of the eastern steps; east-west aligned with the eastern eaves; for sixth rank and below aligned with the eastern rafter; north-south according to hall depth.
translations.idiomatic: On the day itself, rising early, the ablution place was set southeast of the eastern steps—east-west aligned with the eastern eaves for fifth rank and above, aligned with the eastern rafter for sixth rank and below, north-south according to the depth of the hall.

sentences.zh: 罍水在洗東，加勺冪。

translations.literal: The jar of water was east of the ablution place, with ladle and cover added.
translations.idiomatic: The water jar stood east of the ablution place, with ladle and cover placed upon it.

sentences.zh: 篚在洗西南。

translations.literal: The basket was southwest of the ablution place.
translations.idiomatic: The basket was placed southwest of the ablution place.

sentences.zh: 肆實巾一於篚，加冪。

translations.literal: One cloth for drying hands was spread in the basket; cover added.
translations.idiomatic: One cloth for drying the hands was placed in the basket, and a cover was set on top.

sentences.zh: 設席於東房西牖下，陳服於席東，領北上。

translations.literal: A mat was set below the western window of the eastern side room; garments displayed east of the mat, collars to the north.
translations.idiomatic: A mat was set below the western window of the eastern side room, with garments laid out east of the mat, collars facing north.

sentences.zh: 莞筵四，加藻席四，在南。

translations.literal: Four rush mats, plus four embroidered mats, to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Four rush mats with four embroidered mats placed on top, to the south.

sentences.zh: 側尊甒醴在服北，加勺冪，設坫在尊北。

translations.literal: A side wine vessel with black millet ritual wine was north of the garments; ladle and cover added; an offering stand was set north of the vessel.
translations.idiomatic: A side vessel holding black millet ritual wine stood north of the garments, with ladle and cover set upon it; an offering stand was placed north of the vessel.

sentences.zh: 四品以下，設篚無坫，饌陳於坫北。

translations.literal: For fourth rank and below, a basket was set without offering stand; food was displayed north of where the stand would be.
translations.idiomatic: For fourth rank and below, a basket was set but no offering stand; food was displayed to the north.

sentences.zh: 設先於東房，近北。

translations.literal: The ancestral tablet was set in the eastern side room, near the north.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral tablet was set in the eastern side room, near the north wall.

sentences.zh: 罍在洗西，篚在洗東北，肆實以巾。

translations.literal: The water jar was west of the ablution place; the basket northeast of ablution; cloth for drying spread as the item.
translations.idiomatic: The water jar stood west of the ablution place, the basket northeast of it, with the drying cloth placed inside.

sentences.zh: 質明，賓贊至門外，掌次者引之次。

translations.literal: At dawn, guest and announcer arrived outside the gate; the tent master led them to the tent.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the guest and announcer arrived outside the gate; the tent master led them to the tent.

sentences.zh: 賓贊公服，諸行事者各服其服，就位。

translations.literal: Guest and announcer in formal court dress; all functionaries each in their respective dress, took their positions.
translations.idiomatic: The guest and announcer wore formal court dress; each functionary wore his designated garments and took his position.

sentences.zh: 冠各一笥，人執之，侍於西階之西，東面北上。

translations.literal: Each coronet in one box, a person holding it, attending west of the western steps, facing east from north to south.
translations.idiomatic: Each coronet in its own box was held by an attendant and placed west of the western steps, standing facing east from north to south.

sentences.zh: 設主席於阼階上，西面；

translations.literal: The host's mat was set on the eastern steps, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: The host's mat was placed on the eastern steps, facing west;

sentences.zh: 設賓席於西階，東面；

translations.literal: the guest's mat on the western steps, facing east;
translations.idiomatic: the guest's mat on the western steps, facing east;

sentences.zh: 冠者席於主者東北，西面。

translations.literal: the crown-wearer's mat northeast of the host, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: and the crown-wearer's mat northeast of the host, facing west.

sentences.zh: 主者公服立於阼階下，當東序，西面。

translations.literal: The host in formal dress stood below the eastern steps, at the eastern wing, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The host, in formal court dress, stood below the eastern steps at the eastern wing, facing west.

sentences.zh: 諸親公服立於罍洗東南，西面北上。

translations.literal: Relatives in formal dress stood southeast of the water jar and ablution, facing west from north to south.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives in formal court dress stood southeast of the water jar and ablution place, facing west from north to south.

sentences.zh: 尊者在別室。

translations.literal: The honoree was in a separate room.
translations.idiomatic: The honoree waited in a separate room.

sentences.zh: 儐者公服立於門內道東，北面。

translations.literal: The usher in formal dress stood east of the path inside the gate, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The usher, in formal court dress, stood east of the path inside the gate, facing north.

sentences.zh: 冠者雙童髻、空頂幘、雙玉導、彩褶、錦紳、烏皮履，六品以下，導不以玉，立於房中，南面。

translations.literal: The crown-wearer with double child topknots, open-topped headcloth, double jade hairpins, colored pleated robe, brocade sash, black leather shoes; for sixth rank and below, hairpins not of jade; stood in the side room facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The crown-wearer wore double child topknots, an open-topped headcloth, double jade hairpins, a colored pleated robe, brocade sash, and black leather shoes—for sixth rank and below, hairpins without jade—standing in the side room facing south.

sentences.zh: 主者、贊冠者公服立於房內戶東，西面。

translations.literal: Host and crown announcer in formal dress stood east of the door inside the room, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The host and crown announcer, in formal court dress, stood east of the door inside the room, facing west.

sentences.zh: 賓及贊冠者出次，立於門西，東面北上。

translations.literal: Guest and crown announcer came out from the tent, stood west of the gate, facing east from north to south.
translations.idiomatic: The guest and crown announcer emerged from the tent and stood west of the gate, facing east from north to south.

sentences.zh: 儐者進受命，出立門東，西面，曰：「敢請事。

translations.literal: The usher advanced to receive the command, went out and stood east of the gate facing west, and said: "I venture to request the business.
translations.idiomatic: The usher advanced to receive instructions, went out, and stood east of the gate facing west, saying: "I venture to inquire as to the business at hand.

sentences.zh: 」賓曰：「某子有嘉禮，命某執事。

translations.literal: " The guest said: "Such-and-such's son has an auspicious rite; he commands me to officiate.
translations.idiomatic: The guest replied: "Such-and-such's son has an auspicious ceremony; he has commanded me to officiate.

sentences.zh: 」儐者入告，主者迎賓於大門外之東，西面，再拜，賓答拜。

translations.literal: " The usher entered and reported; the host received the guest east outside the great gate, facing west; both performed two bows; the guest returned the bow.
